title: When puberty is late enough to evaluate
lead: Evaluate no breast development by age 13, no menarche by age 15, or no testicular enlargement by age 14.
lines: Those ages start the workup. They are not themselves a diagnosis.
Constitutional delay is a diagnosis of exclusion after the exam, the growth curve, and the indicated labs.
A girl who started breasts and has no period three years later is also late, even if she is not yet 15.
miss: Reassuring a 15-year-old with no periods because a cousin was a late bloomer.

source.name: StatPearls. Delayed Puberty.
source.says: The chapter gives the ages at which absent pubertal landmarks should be evaluated rather than watched.

title: Ambiguous genitalia can be salt-wasting disease
lead: A newborn with atypical genitalia is evaluated for salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia before the baby goes home.
lines: The dangerous enzyme defect loses aldosterone. The sodium falls and the potassium rises in the first weeks, not always on day one.
17-hydroxyprogesterone is the test for 21-hydroxylase deficiency.
Do not assign a sex in the hallway.
miss: Discharging a virilized infant with no electrolyte plan and no steroid plan.

source.name: StatPearls. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
source.says: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency presents in early infancy. Electrolytes and 17-hydroxyprogesterone are obtained before reassurance.

title: Turner syndrome is followed for the aorta and the growth
lead: A girl with Turner syndrome gets blood-pressure checks, aortic imaging, and a growth conversation. The karyotype is not the end of the visit.
lines: Coarctation and a bicuspid valve are what you listen and image for.
The kidneys are imaged once.
Estrogen is replaced at the time of puberty, with a specialist, because the streak gonads will not produce it.
miss: Measuring height once and never taking a blood pressure in the legs.

source.name: StatPearls. Turner Syndrome.
source.says: Cardiac lesions, renal anomalies, and absent puberty are the follow-up. The karyotype starts that plan.

title: Klinefelter syndrome is treated as hypogonadism
lead: Men with Klinefelter syndrome and low testosterone are offered testosterone replacement. The infertility is a separate conversation and is not fixed by the gel.
lines: Small firm testes are the exam.
Breast tissue is examined because the cancer risk is higher.
Learning differences are supported. They are not the reason to withhold hormone treatment.
miss: Telling the patient testosterone will restore sperm.

source.name: StatPearls. Klinefelter Syndrome.
source.says: Testosterone treats the hypogonadism. It does not restore fertility.

title: DiGeorge is calcium, infection, and the heart
lead: A newborn with DiGeorge features gets a calcium, an immune evaluation, and a heart evaluation. The low calcium can be the first seizure.
lines: Irradiated blood is used if a transfusion is needed and the immune defect is not yet clear.
Live vaccines wait until the immune status is known.
The face and the outflow murmur are the clues to order those tests.
miss: Treating a neonatal seizure with an antiseizure drug and never checking the calcium.

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroanatomy, Neural Crest.
source.says: The clinical dangers are hypocalcemia, infection from thymic absence, and a conotruncal heart defect.

title: TTP is not a platelet order
lead: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a medical emergency treated with plasma exchange. Platelets are for life-threatening bleeding, not for the number.
lines: The picture is microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and organ injury, often neurologic or renal.
ADAMTS13 activity is the confirmatory test. Do not wait for it to start plasma exchange when the picture is classic.
ITP is a different disease: low platelets, no schistocytes, and no hemolysis.
miss: Transfusing platelets to a safe number before plasma exchange and seeding more microvascular thrombi.

source.name: StatPearls. Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura.
source.says: Plasma exchange is the urgent treatment. Platelet transfusion is reserved for serious bleeding.

title: Febrile neutropenia does not wait for the culture
lead: Fever with an absolute neutrophil count under 500 needs an antipseudomonal antibiotic within an hour of recognition.
lines: Draw cultures first only if doing so does not delay the antibiotic.
Monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam is the start for most stable patients.
Add vancomycin for a specific reason: suspected catheter infection, skin or soft-tissue infection, hemodynamic instability, or known resistant gram-positive colonization. Not for every fever.
miss: Adding vancomycin to every neutropenic fever, or holding antibiotics until the neutrophil count is repeated.

source.name: StatPearls. Febrile Neutropenia.
source.says: Prompt antipseudomonal therapy is the time-critical action. Vancomycin is added for listed indications, not by reflex.

title: Acute chest syndrome is more than pain medicine
lead: Acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease is a new infiltrate with chest pain, fever, or hypoxia. Incentive spirometry prevents it, and severe disease is an exchange-transfusion conversation.
lines: Antibiotics cover community pneumonia while you treat the sickle crisis.
Simple transfusion is for a drop in hemoglobin. Exchange is for the severe respiratory failure.
Pain control that lets the patient take deep breaths is part of the prevention.
miss: Discharging a hypoxic sickle-cell patient with oral opioids and no film.

source.name: StatPearls. Sickle Cell Disease.
source.says: Acute chest syndrome is treated in the hospital. Incentive spirometry reduces chest complications of a pain crisis.

title: Bleeding ITP is treated. A number alone may not be
lead: Immune thrombocytopenia is treated when there is bleeding or a procedure, not because every low number must be normalized today.
lines: Steroids or IVIG are the usual first treatments when treatment is indicated.
Platelets are for serious bleeding, and they do not stick around.
TTP is excluded by the smear. Schistocytes change the disease.
miss: Transfusing platelets every day to keep a count above 50 in a patient who is not bleeding.

source.name: StatPearls. Immune Thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Treatment is driven by bleeding and by the need for a procedure. Platelet transfusion is for serious bleeding.

title: A hemophilia bleed gets factor, not fresh frozen plasma as the plan
lead: A joint or muscle bleed in hemophilia A is treated with factor VIII replacement. Fresh frozen plasma is not the outpatient plan.
lines: The dose follows the site. A head bleed is 100% replacement and imaging.
A mixing study that no longer corrects means an inhibitor.
Avoid intramuscular injections and NSAIDs.
miss: Sending a hemarthrosis home on ibuprofen.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemophilia A.
source.says: Factor VIII replacement treats the bleed. Head trauma is treated as a bleed until imaging and factor say otherwise.

title: Desmopressin is for type 1 von Willebrand, not type 2B
lead: Type 1 von Willebrand disease can be treated with desmopressin before a procedure. Type 2B can worsen because the abnormal multimer binds platelets.
lines: Know the subtype before the drug.
Antifibrinolytics help mucosal bleeding.
Factor replacement that contains von Willebrand factor is the alternative when desmopressin is unsafe.
miss: Giving desmopressin to every patient with the disease name and watching the platelet count fall.

source.name: StatPearls. Von Willebrand Disease.
source.says: Desmopressin is appropriate for many type 1 patients and is contraindicated in type 2B.

title: DIC is treated by treating the cause
lead: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is treated by treating the cause. Blood products are for bleeding or a procedure, not for a daily number.
lines: Cryoprecipitate replaces fibrinogen.
Platelets are for bleeding.
Heparin is a selected choice in a clotting-predominant patient, not the first syringe in a patient who is bleeding.
miss: Heparinizing a bleeding obstetric patient whose fibrinogen is 60.

source.name: StatPearls. Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation.
source.says: The cause is the treatment. Replacement of fibrinogen and platelets is for bleeding or invasive procedures.

title: Do not start warfarin alone for HIT
lead: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is treated by stopping all heparin and starting a non-heparin anticoagulant. Warfarin alone is dangerous in the acute phase.
lines: Argatroban or another direct thrombin inhibitor is the usual bridge.
Platelet transfusion is not the treatment of the low count.
The fall begins 5 to 10 days after exposure, or sooner on re-exposure.
miss: Transfusing platelets and continuing the heparin because the circuit is clotting.

source.name: StatPearls. Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
source.says: All heparin is stopped. A non-heparin anticoagulant is started. Warfarin monotherapy in acute HIT can cause venous limb gangrene.

title: Established tumor lysis with a high uric acid gets rasburicase
lead: Allopurinol prevents new uric acid. Rasburicase breaks down uric acid that is already there. A high uric acid with tumor lysis gets rasburicase if it is available.
lines: Fluids are started in everyone at risk.
Screen for G6PD deficiency before rasburicase when you can. The drug can hemolyze those patients.
The potassium is the immediate threat on the monitor.
miss: Starting only allopurinol when the uric acid is already 14 and the potassium is 6.

source.name: StatPearls. Tumor Lysis Syndrome.
source.says: Rasburicase lowers existing uric acid. Allopurinol only reduces formation. Fluids and potassium management come with either drug.

title: Phlebotomy is the treatment of polycythemia vera
lead: Polycythemia vera is treated by phlebotomy to lower the hematocrit, plus aspirin when the diagnosis is secure and the platelets are not extreme.
lines: A high erythropoietin is not this disease. Do not phlebotomize hypoxic lung disease down to an unsafe hematocrit.
Hydroxyurea is added for high-risk patients.
Aquagenic itching is a clue, not a dermatology referral alone.
miss: Phlebotomizing a patient with a high EPO from lung disease to a hematocrit of 40.

source.name: StatPearls. Polycythemia Vera.
source.says: Phlebotomy lowers the hematocrit in polycythemia vera. Secondary erythrocytosis is not treated the same way.

title: Start ATRA when the smear says promyelocytic leukemia
lead: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is treated with all-trans retinoic acid as soon as the diagnosis is suspected. Do not wait for the karyotype if the smear and the coagulopathy match.
lines: The early death is bleeding. Correct the coagulopathy.
Differentiation syndrome is fever and pulmonary infiltrates after the drug starts. It is treated, not ignored.
Arsenic trioxide is part of modern regimens. The point for this bite is not to delay the differentiating agent.
miss: Waiting three days for cytogenetics while the fibrinogen falls.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
source.says: All-trans retinoic acid is started when acute promyelocytic leukemia is suspected, because early bleeding death occurs before confirmatory genetics return.

title: PNH with hemolysis or thrombosis gets a complement inhibitor
lead: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria with hemolysis or thrombosis is treated with a complement inhibitor. Anticoagulation alone does not stop the complement.
lines: Unusual-site thrombosis is this disease until the flow cytometry is back.
Iron is lost in the urine. Replace it if the patient is deficient. Do not assume the anemia is iron overload.
Eculizumab raises the Neisseria risk. Vaccinate.
miss: Anticoagulating a hepatic-vein thrombosis and never ordering the flow cytometry.

source.name: StatPearls. Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
source.says: Complement inhibition treats the hemolysis. Meningococcal vaccination is required because terminal complement is blocked.

title: A hemolytic transfusion reaction stops the unit
lead: Fever, pain, or dark urine during a transfusion stops that unit. Do not slow it and watch.
lines: Check the identity of the patient and the bag. Clerical error is the classic cause.
Support the pressure and the urine output.
A febrile nonhemolytic reaction is a diagnosis you make after hemolysis is unlikely, not before you stop the blood.
miss: Restarting the same unit after acetaminophen.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.
source.says: The transfusion is stopped at the first sign of acute hemolysis. The unit and a new sample return to the blood bank.

title: Either thrombolytic, inside 4.5 hours
lead: For an eligible adult within 4.5 hours, give tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg up to 25 mg, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg.
lines: Disabling deficit is the indication. A low NIHSS score does not cancel it.
Do not use advanced imaging to withhold treatment inside 4.5 hours.
Tenecteplase 0.4 mg/kg is not the dose in this window.
miss: Waiting for an MRI, or quoting only alteplase, in a patient who is already inside the window.
diagramAlt: Inside 4.5 hours, tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg up to 25 mg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg. Blood pressure before treatment is below 185 over 110.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: The guideline endorses either tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (maximum 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90 mg) within 4.5 hours, without advanced-imaging selection.

title: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepine first
lead: A seizure that continues, or that recurs without recovery, gets a benzodiazepine now. The second drug is not another benzodiazepine.
lines: Give IV lorazepam, or IM midazolam if there is no IV.
If it continues, give one adequate dose of fosphenytoin, valproate, or levetiracetam. Those three are equivalent as the next drug.
Do not stack small benzodiazepine doses and call that treatment.
miss: Starting a phenytoin load while the first benzodiazepine dose was never given.

source.name: StatPearls. Status Epilepticus. ESETT, New England Journal of Medicine, 2019.
source.says: First-line treatment is a benzodiazepine. ESETT found levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, and valproate equivalent as the next intravenous drug.

more.name: Kapur et al. Randomized Trial of Three Anticonvulsant Medications. N Engl J Med. 2019.

title: Thunderclap headache is a bleed until it is not
lead: A headache that is maximal at onset gets a noncontrast head CT now. A negative early CT does not close the question.
lines: Do the CT before the neurology consult and before a migraine cocktail.
If the CT is negative and the story is still a thunderclap in the first hours, the next test is lumbar puncture or a vascular study, based on timing and availability.
Exertion, pregnancy, a focal deficit, fever with neck stiffness, cancer, or immunosuppression also moves imaging up. A stable recurrent migraine does not.
miss: Sending the patient home because the CT was read overnight as negative and nobody asked how the headache started.

source.name: StatPearls. Thunderclap Headache.
source.says: Thunderclap onset requires emergent imaging for subarachnoid hemorrhage. A negative CT does not end the evaluation when the pretest probability remains high.

title: Dexamethasone before the meningitis antibiotic
lead: In adults with suspected pneumococcal meningitis, give dexamethasone before or with the first antibiotic dose.
lines: The point is to blunt the inflammatory burst as bacteria lyse. After the antibiotic is already in, the window is gone.
Do not delay the antibiotic for a CT if there is no indication for CT. Blood cultures, then drug, then the puncture if imaging has to come first.
Stop the steroid if the organism is not Streptococcus pneumoniae, unless another indication exists.
miss: Hanging the antibiotic, then remembering the steroid an hour later.

source.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis.
source.says: The IDSA adult guideline recommends dexamethasone before or with the first dose when pneumococcal meningitis is suspected. This remains the standing IDSA guideline.

title: Guillain-Barré is IVIG or exchange, not prednisone
lead: Guillain-Barré syndrome is treated with intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange. Steroids do not help.
lines: Watch the vital capacity and the negative inspiratory force. The diaphragm fails quietly.
A spinal fluid full of cells is not this disease.
Campylobacter is the infection to ask about, and it does not change the first treatment.
miss: Starting high-dose prednisone for ascending paralysis.

source.name: StatPearls. Guillain-Barre Syndrome.
source.says: IVIG or plasma exchange is the disease-modifying treatment. Corticosteroids are not effective.

title: An acute multiple-sclerosis flare gets a steroid, not an antibiotic
lead: A new disabling multiple-sclerosis flare is treated with high-dose corticosteroids. An antibiotic does not treat a demyelinating plaque.
lines: Infection can worsen old symptoms without a new plaque. Look for it before you call every worsening a flare.
Disease-modifying therapy is the long plan and is not the same syringe as the flare steroid.
Optic neuritis is this conversation, and vision is followed.
miss: Giving antibiotics for a sensory level and a clear urine.

source.name: StatPearls. Multiple Sclerosis.
source.says: Acute disabling relapses are treated with corticosteroids. Disease-modifying therapy is a separate long-term decision.

title: Levodopa is the most effective drug for Parkinson motor symptoms
lead: When Parkinson disease limits function, levodopa is the most effective drug for the motor symptoms. Saving it for late disease is an old idea.
lines: Carbidopa is given with it so less is lost in the periphery.
A dopamine blocker on the medication list is stopped before the diagnosis is locked.
Impulse-control problems are the agonist story. Ask about gambling and sex.
miss: Withholding levodopa for years from a patient who can no longer walk, out of fear of it wearing off.

source.name: StatPearls. Parkinson Disease.
source.says: Levodopa is the most effective medication for motor symptoms. Dopamine-blocking drugs are stopped because they mimic the disease.

title: Absence epilepsy is ethosuximide
lead: Ethosuximide is the drug for childhood absence seizures. Carbamazepine can worsen them.
lines: There is no postictal confusion. A confused child had a different seizure.
Hyperventilation can reproduce the spell in the office.
A child who also has generalized convulsions needs a drug that covers both, which ethosuximide does not.
miss: Starting carbamazepine for staring spells.

source.name: StatPearls. Absence Seizure.
source.says: Ethosuximide is first-line for absence. Some sodium-channel drugs worsen absence seizures.

title: Carbamazepine is first for trigeminal neuralgia
lead: Trigeminal neuralgia is treated with carbamazepine. A dental extraction is not the treatment of electric pain.
lines: Check sodium and watch for rash.
Sensory loss or a young patient gets imaging.
A continuous burning pain is a different diagnosis.
miss: Pulling a tooth for seconds of shock-like pain in the cheek.

source.name: StatPearls. Trigeminal Neuralgia.
source.says: Carbamazepine is the first-line drug. Imaging is added when the story is atypical.

title: Stop the antipsychotic in neuroleptic malignant syndrome
lead: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is treated by stopping the dopamine blocker, cooling, and supporting the pressure. Another dose of the same drug is not the treatment of the agitation.
lines: Creatine kinase is high and the reflexes are not clonus.
A benzodiazepine can help agitation. The antipsychotic does not.
Restarting a drug later, if ever, is a specialist decision at a low dose.
miss: Increasing the antipsychotic because the patient is more confused.

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
source.says: The offending dopamine antagonist is stopped. Supportive care is the treatment. More of the drug worsens the syndrome.

title: Stop the serotonergic drugs
lead: Serotonin syndrome is treated by stopping the serotonergic drugs and giving a benzodiazepine for agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antidote when supportive care is not enough.
lines: The combination is often an SSRI plus an MAOI, a triptan, tramadol, or linezolid.
Clonus is the sign that separates it from neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
It starts in hours, so today's new prescription is the cause.
miss: Adding linezolid to an SSRI and treating the shivering as influenza.

source.name: StatPearls. Serotonin Syndrome.
source.says: Offending drugs are stopped. Benzodiazepines treat agitation, and cyproheptadine is the serotonin antagonist used when needed.

title: A high lithium level is held, and severe toxicity is dialyzed
lead: Hold lithium and check the level when tremor, confusion, or a drug interaction appears. Severe neurotoxicity or a very high level is dialyzed.
lines: NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE inhibitors, and dehydration raise the level.
Intravenous saline is for volume depletion. It is not a substitute for dialysis in severe toxicity.
The level can be drawn too early and look lower than the tissue burden.
miss: Continuing the lithium and adding ibuprofen for the tremor.

source.name: StatPearls. Lithium Toxicity.
source.says: Lithium is held. Severe toxicity is treated with hemodialysis. Interacting drugs are stopped.

title: Do not treat tardive dyskinesia with a higher dose as the plan
lead: Tardive dyskinesia is managed by reassessing the antipsychotic, not by raising a first-generation drug. A VMAT2 inhibitor is the specific treatment.
lines: Acute dystonia is the opposite time course and answers to an anticholinergic.
The movements can persist after the drug stops. Warn the patient.
Akathisia is restlessness and is a different dose change.
miss: Doubling haloperidol for mouth movements that started after a year of haloperidol.

source.name: StatPearls. Tardive Dyskinesia.
source.says: VMAT2 inhibitors treat tardive dyskinesia. Increasing the causative antipsychotic is not the treatment.

title: Bell palsy gets a steroid early and eye protection
lead: Idiopathic Bell palsy is treated with oral corticosteroids within the first few days. The eye that does not close is lubricated.
lines: Forehead involvement is what makes it peripheral. Forehead sparing is a stroke.
Vesicles in the ear are zoster and a different antiviral decision.
Antiviral therapy is added in severe palsy, not as the only drug.
miss: Sending a forehead-sparing droop home with artificial tears.

source.name: StatPearls. Bell Palsy.
source.says: Corticosteroids are started early. Corneal protection is part of the visit. Forehead sparing is not Bell palsy.

title: A deteriorating epidural hematoma goes to surgery
lead: An epidural hematoma in a patient who is worsening goes to surgical evacuation. The lucid interval is the time you still have.
lines: A lens-shaped bleed on CT in a declining patient is not a medical admission.
Reverse anticoagulation if it is present.
A stable tiny collection can be watched by a neurosurgeon. The declining patient cannot.
miss: Admitting a dilating pupil to the floor for serial exams overnight.

source.name: StatPearls. Epidural Hematoma.
source.says: Clinical deterioration is an indication for evacuation. Observation is only for a carefully selected stable patient.

title: A large or symptomatic subdural hematoma is surgical
lead: A subdural hematoma that shifts the brain or worsens the exam is evacuated. Anticoagulation is reversed.
lines: Older patients can have a large collection and a mild first complaint. The scan decides the size.
A small chronic collection without mass effect can be followed.
Do not restart the anticoagulant the same evening without a plan.
miss: Restarting warfarin the night of the fall because the patient has atrial fibrillation and the CT was not yet done.

source.name: StatPearls. Subdural Hematoma.
source.says: Mass effect and neurologic worsening are surgical. Anticoagulation is reversed and not reflexively restarted.

title: Cerebellar hemorrhage is a surgical conversation
lead: A cerebellar hemorrhage that compresses the brainstem or blocks the ventricle is evacuated. Do not watch it on the floor.
lines: The signs are headache, vomiting, and ataxia, then a falling level of consciousness.
Blood pressure is lowered into the range the hemorrhagic-stroke guidance uses, without dropping perfusion.
A deep small bleed in the putamen is a different surgical decision from the cerebellum.
miss: Waiting for the patient to become comatose before calling neurosurgery.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemorrhagic Stroke Overview.
source.says: Cerebellar hemorrhage with compression or hydrocephalus is evacuated. Delay until coma worsens the outcome.

title: Do not use a triptan in coronary disease
lead: A triptan treats migraine early. It is contraindicated in coronary disease, uncontrolled hypertension, and with recent ergot or another triptan.
lines: The headache of thunderclap onset is not migraine until the bleed is excluded.
Medication-overuse headache is a near-daily painkiller, and the treatment is to stop it.
A new neurologic deficit during the headache is not a routine refill.
miss: Giving sumatriptan to a patient with ongoing chest pain.

source.name: StatPearls. Migraine Headache.
source.says: Triptans are contraindicated in coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease and with recent ergot use.

title: Stop the anticholinergic in a patient with dementia
lead: Anticholinergic drugs worsen Alzheimer disease. A cholinesterase inhibitor is a modest symptomatic drug, not a cure, and it fights the anticholinergic.
lines: A sudden confusion is delirium until the cause is found. It is not a dose increase of the dementia drug.
Frontotemporal change is a different disease and does not answer to the same drug.
Caregiver support and safety are the treatment that matters as much as the pill.
miss: Adding diphenhydramine for sleep in a patient who is already losing memory.

source.name: StatPearls. Alzheimer Disease.
source.says: Anticholinergics worsen cognition. Cholinesterase inhibitors are symptomatic and are not combined with an anticholinergic load.

title: A shunt helps normal-pressure hydrocephalus when gait leads
lead: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus is considered for a shunt when gait is the leading problem and a tap improves it. A cortical dementia is not shunted.
lines: The order of symptoms matters: gait, then bladder, then mind.
Large ventricles with little cortical atrophy are the scan.
A patient whose memory failed first is not this disease.
miss: Shunting a patient with years of isolated memory loss.

source.name: StatPearls. Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus.
source.says: Gait-predominant disease that improves with CSF removal is the patient considered for shunting.

title: A large brain abscess is drained
lead: A brain abscess that is large or not responding is drained. Antibiotics alone are for a small abscess in a patient you can follow.
lines: The source, ear, sinus, or heart, is treated too.
Steroids are for significant edema, not for every ring.
A lumbar puncture is not how you make this diagnosis.
miss: Six weeks of antibiotics and no drainage for a 4-centimeter lesion with a worsening exam.

source.name: StatPearls. Brain Abscess.
source.says: Large abscesses are drained. Antibiotics cover the source. Lumbar puncture is avoided when mass effect is present.

title: Horner syndrome gets a carotid and an apex
lead: A painful Horner syndrome is a carotid dissection until imaged. A painless one in a smoker includes the lung apex.
lines: The pupil is small. Do not start pilocarpine thinking it is a dilated pupil.
A brainstem stroke can cause it with other signs. Those signs decide the scanner.
An isolated chronic Horner still gets an explanation.
miss: Calling a painful small pupil a migraine and sending the patient home.

source.name: StatPearls. Horner Syndrome.
source.says: Acute painful Horner syndrome is imaged for carotid dissection. A lung apex lesion is sought when the story is a smoker.

title: A TIA is a stroke warning, not a cleared patient
lead: A transient ischemic attack is treated as a threatened stroke. Antiplatelet therapy, a cause, and a same-day or next-day plan are the visit.
lines: Atrial fibrillation found on the tracing changes the drug to anticoagulation.
A high-grade carotid stenosis is a surgical conversation.
The symptoms resolving does not mean the risk resolved.
miss: Reassuring a patient whose hand weakness resolved and scheduling clinic in a month.

source.name: StatPearls. Transient Ischemic Attack.
source.says: TIA is a neurologic emergency. Antithrombotic therapy and a search for a cardioembolic or carotid source happen immediately.

title: Cord compression gets steroids and a surgeon or radiation
lead: Spinal cord compression is dexamethasone and urgent decompression or radiation. Plain films are not the test.
lines: Back pain plus a sensory level, bilateral weakness, or new bladder failure is the syndrome.
MRI is the image.
Cancer is the common cause in an adult. Treat the cord before the staging is complete.
miss: Ordering outpatient lumbar films for a patient who cannot urinate.

source.name: StatPearls. Spinal Cord Compression.
source.says: High-dose dexamethasone and urgent surgical or radiation decompression are the treatment. MRI is the imaging test.

title: Do not image ordinary back pain
lead: Acute low back pain without a red flag does not get imaging in the first six weeks.
lines: Red flags that change the plan: cancer history, unexplained weight loss, fever, injection-drug use, recent spinal infection or bacteremia, trauma, progressive deficit, saddle anesthesia, or new bowel or bladder loss.
Cauda equina is an MRI and a surgical call, not a course of ibuprofen.
Early imaging without a flag finds incidental disease and does not speed recovery.
miss: Ordering an MRI for two days of mechanical pain because the patient asked for one.

source.name: ACP Clinical Practice Guideline. Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain.
source.says: Clinicians should not obtain imaging for low back pain in the absence of red flags. Most acute pain improves without it.

title: Treat the gout flare
lead: A gout flare is treated with colchicine, an NSAID, or a glucocorticoid. Allopurinol alone is not the treatment of the flare.
lines: Pick the anti-inflammatory the kidneys, the stomach, and the other drugs allow.
If the patient is already on urate-lowering therapy, do not stop it for the flare.
Opioids do not treat the inflammation.
miss: Starting allopurinol during a hot joint and sending the patient home on that alone.

source.name: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout.
source.says: Anti-inflammatory therapy treats the flare. Urate-lowering therapy is the long plan and is not a substitute for treating the flare.

title: Fasciotomy is the treatment of a tight compartment
lead: Acute compartment syndrome is opened. Analgesia and elevation do not replace the fasciotomy.
lines: Pain on passive stretch is enough to call the surgeon. A pulse can still be present.
Remove the cast or the dressing first if that is the cause, and reassess immediately.
The limb is not observed overnight once the diagnosis is made.
miss: Increasing the opioid and rechecking the compartment in the morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Compartment Syndrome and Fasciotomy.
source.says: Fasciotomy is definitive treatment. A present pulse does not exclude the diagnosis.

title: Inflammatory back pain is treated with an NSAID and movement
lead: Ankylosing spondylitis is treated with an NSAID and with activity. Rest is the wrong prescription.
lines: A TNF inhibitor is the next step when NSAIDs fail and the diagnosis is secure.
Uveitis is treated as uveitis, urgently, not with the same oral NSAID plan alone.
A young man whose pain is worse in the morning is not given six weeks of bed rest.
miss: Prescribing bed rest for morning stiffness that improves with walking.

source.name: StatPearls. Ankylosing Spondylitis.
source.says: NSAIDs and exercise are first-line. Prolonged rest worsens inflammatory back pain.

title: Adult dermatomyositis gets a cancer search
lead: Adult dermatomyositis is treated with immunosuppression and is searched for cancer. The rash is not sent to dermatology alone.
lines: Proximal weakness is the function you measure.
Interstitial lung disease is asked about and imaged when the story fits.
A statin myopathy has no Gottron papules. Stop the statin, but do not miss the rash.
miss: Prescribing a topical steroid for Gottron papules and ignoring the shoulders.

source.name: StatPearls. Dermatomyositis.
source.says: Immunosuppression treats the muscle and skin. Adult disease prompts a search for an associated malignancy.

title: Psoriatic arthritis is treated as a joint disease
lead: Psoriatic arthritis is treated even when the skin is mild. A TNF inhibitor or another targeted drug is used when NSAIDs are not enough.
lines: Dactylitis and DIP disease are the clues on the exam.
Nail pitting counts. Ask the patient to show the scalp.
Methotrexate is a common conventional drug. It is not the only option when the joints are eroding.
miss: Treating only the skin plaques while the digit stays swollen.

source.name: StatPearls. Psoriatic Arthritis.
source.says: Joint disease is treated on its own. Skin clearance does not guarantee the arthritis is controlled.

title: Reactive arthritis: treat the germ if it is still there
lead: A persistent triggering infection is treated. The sterile joint itself is treated with an NSAID, not with weeks of unnecessary broad antibiotics.
lines: A tap that is culture-negative is the point.
Uveitis needs an eye exam.
A single dose of antibiotics does not fix established joint inflammation.
miss: Operating a culture-negative knee or giving a month of vancomycin.

source.name: StatPearls. Reactive Arthritis.
source.says: The joint is sterile. Treat a still-present infection and use anti-inflammatory therapy for the arthritis.

title: Marfan syndrome is followed at the aortic root
lead: Marfan syndrome is followed with aortic-root imaging. A beta blocker or an angiotensin-receptor blocker is used to slow growth. The long fingers are not the follow-up.
lines: Surgery is planned from the diameter and the family history, not from a symptom of rupture.
Pregnancy is a high-risk aortic state and is planned.
Contact sports are restricted when the aorta is dilated.
miss: Reassuring a click and never measuring the root.

source.name: StatPearls. Marfan Syndrome.
source.says: Aortic-root surveillance and blood-pressure lowering drugs are the medical plan. Diameter drives the surgical timing.

title: Pemphigus is a steroid disease and the mouth is involved
lead: Pemphigus vulgaris is treated with systemic corticosteroids and a steroid-sparing drug. The mouth erosions are part of the disease, not a separate thrush.
lines: Nikolsky-positive flaccid bullae are the exam.
Fluid and wound care matter because the skin barrier is gone.
Bullous pemphigoid is tense and is a different, usually less mucosal, disease.
miss: Prescribing nystatin alone for months of oral erosions and skin loss.

source.name: StatPearls. Pemphigus Vulgaris.
source.says: Systemic immunosuppression is required. Mucosal erosions are expected and are not treated as isolated candidiasis.

title: A septic native joint is washed and covered for staph
lead: After the tap, a septic native joint is washed and treated with antibiotics that cover Staphylococcus aureus until the culture narrows them.
lines: Gonorrhea is the exception to think of in a young sexually active patient, and the culture includes it.
A prosthetic joint is a different operation and a different biofilm regimen.
Oral step-down happens after the source is controlled, not on day one of a toxic patient.
miss: Leaving a purulent knee on intravenous antibiotics without drainage.

source.name: StatPearls. Septic Arthritis.
source.says: Drainage plus antistaphylococcal antibiotics is the treatment of native-joint septic arthritis. Culture narrows the drug.

title: Hip fracture is operated early and protected from clot
lead: A hip fracture in an older adult is operated as soon as the patient is medically ready, generally within a day or two, and is given clot prophylaxis.
lines: Pain is treated so the patient can move. Delirium is prevented by that, by glasses, and by not adding anticholinergics.
A fragility fracture means treat the osteoporosis. Do not wait for an outpatient DEXA to name the disease.
Urinary catheters come out.
miss: Waiting a week for the internist to clear a stable patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Hip Fracture Overview.
source.says: Early surgery and venous-thromboembolism prophylaxis are the plan. A fragility fracture is treated as osteoporosis.

title: Osteogenesis imperfecta does not cancel a child-protection question
lead: Fractures from osteogenesis imperfecta are real, and inflicted injury is still considered. Blue sclerae do not end the duty to protect a child.
lines: The pattern of the fracture, the history, and the developmental stage are the questions.
Both diagnoses can be true.
Hearing and dental findings support the collagen disease and are documented.
miss: Closing a child-protection evaluation because the sclerae are blue.

source.name: StatPearls. Osteogenesis Imperfecta.
source.says: Brittle-bone disease explains some fractures and does not exclude inflicted trauma. Both are assessed.

title: Necrotizing infection goes to the operating room
lead: Necrotizing fasciitis is taken to surgery when it is suspected. Broad antibiotics start on the way. Imaging that delays the room is the miss.
lines: Pain past the visible skin and a toxic patient are enough.
Group A streptococcus and mixed organisms are both covered until the culture returns.
A stable cellulitis with a clear border is the disease you do not take to surgery.
miss: Ordering a CT and a 24-hour antibiotic trial for a toxic patient with pain out of proportion.

source.name: StatPearls. Necrotizing Fasciitis.
source.says: Suspected necrotizing infection is a surgical emergency. Antibiotics are started and do not replace debridement.

title: The ACS clocks
lead: A 12-lead ECG is due within 10 minutes of first medical contact. A STEMI does not wait for the troponin.
lines: STEMI goes to a PCI-capable hospital. The system goal is first medical contact to device in 90 minutes.
If the patient arrives at a hospital that cannot do PCI, the transfer goal is 120 minutes. If that will be missed, give fibrinolysis.
A nondiagnostic first ECG with ongoing pain gets serial ECGs, including posterior leads when the story fits.
miss: Waiting for a troponin before activating the lab for ST elevation.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: Acquire and interpret a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Primary PCI targets are 90 minutes at a PCI-capable hospital and 120 minutes when transfer is required.

title: The four pillars, and the improved EF
lead: HFrEF gets all four: an ARNI, an evidence-based beta blocker, a mineralocorticoid antagonist, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
lines: The evidence-based beta blockers are carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol.
If the EF later rises above 40%, this is improved EF. Keep the HFrEF drugs.
A small rise in creatinine after the start is expected. It is not, by itself, a reason to stop the drug that keeps the patient alive.
miss: Stopping the ACE inhibitor or the ARNI because the creatinine rose from 1.1 to 1.3, and never restarting it.
diagramAlt: Four pillars for HFrEF: ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker, mineralocorticoid antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor. Improved ejection fraction stays on this therapy.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: Guideline-directed therapy for HFrEF is four drug classes, including an SGLT2 inhibitor. Patients with improved EF continue HFrEF treatment. Reaffirmed as current in 2025.

title: Who with atrial fibrillation gets an anticoagulant
lead: Anticoagulate when the yearly stroke risk is about 2% or higher. For CHA2DS2-VASc, that is 2 or more in men and 3 or more in women.
lines: Use a DOAC rather than warfarin unless there is moderate or severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve.
The pattern of the fibrillation, paroxysmal or permanent, does not change the indication.
Aspirin is not stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation.
miss: Prescribing aspirin because the CHA2DS2-VASc score felt too low for a DOAC, or withholding a DOAC because the patient is often in sinus rhythm.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Class 1 anticoagulation starts at an estimated yearly risk of at least 2%. DOACs are preferred except for moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis and mechanical valves.

title: Stage 2 hypertension starts two drugs
lead: In the 2025 blood-pressure guideline, a pressure of 140/90 or higher starts two agents from different classes, preferably in one pill.
lines: The treatment goal for most adults is under 130/80, and a higher-risk patient is encouraged toward a systolic pressure under 120.
Risk is estimated with PREVENT, not the old pooled cohort equation.
Stage 1 with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or a 10-year risk of at least 7.5% starts a drug. Lower risk gets 3 to 6 months of lifestyle first.
miss: Starting one drug at 162/98 and rechecking in six months.

source.name: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline.
source.says: Stage 2 hypertension is treated with two agents. The goal is under 130/80, using the PREVENT equations for risk.

title: Do not give thrombolysis for a STEMI you can open
lead: A STEMI that can reach a PCI-capable lab within the time goal goes to PCI, not to fibrinolysis.
lines: First medical contact to device is 90 minutes at a PCI hospital and 120 minutes if transfer is required.
If that transfer will miss 120 minutes, give a fibrinolytic and do not keep waiting.
A posterior lead and a repeat ECG catch the STEMI the first tracing missed.
miss: Giving a fibrinolytic in the parking lot of a PCI hospital.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: Primary PCI is preferred when the system can meet the 90- or 120-minute goal. Fibrinolysis is for when that goal will be missed.

title: Oxygen in ACS is for hypoxia, not for the diagnosis
lead: A patient with suspected ACS and a normal oxygen saturation does not get routine oxygen.
lines: Give oxygen when the saturation is low or the patient is in distress from hypoxia.
Aspirin, if there is no allergy or active bleeding, is the drug that is actually indicated.
A STEMI still does not wait for the troponin.
miss: Putting every chest-pain patient on a nonrebreather.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: Routine oxygen is not recommended when saturation is normal. Reperfusion and aspirin are the time-critical actions.

title: Improved ejection fraction stays on the four drugs
lead: If the ejection fraction was 40% or lower and later rises, keep the HFrEF drugs. This is improved ejection fraction, not a cure.
lines: Stopping the ARNI or the beta blocker because the number looks better is how patients bounce back.
A small creatinine rise after the start is expected.
The evidence-based beta blockers remain carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol.
miss: Declaring the heart failure gone because the ejection fraction is now 45%.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: Patients with improved ejection fraction continue guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF.

title: Cardioversion does not cancel the anticoagulant
lead: Restoring sinus rhythm does not remove the stroke risk that required anticoagulation.
lines: The indication is the yearly risk, not the rhythm on today's ECG.
A DOAC is preferred unless there is moderate or severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve.
Aspirin is not the substitute.
miss: Stopping the DOAC the week after a successful cardioversion.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Stroke prevention is based on risk, not on whether the patient is currently in sinus rhythm.

title: A mechanical valve or mitral stenosis still gets warfarin
lead: A DOAC is not the anticoagulant for moderate or severe mitral stenosis or for a mechanical valve. Those patients get warfarin.
lines: The rest of nonvalvular atrial fibrillation prefers a DOAC.
A bioprosthetic valve is not the same instruction as a mechanical valve.
The INR target follows the valve, not a guess of 2 to 3 for every prosthesis.
miss: Switching a mechanical mitral valve to apixaban because the patient dislikes blood tests.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: DOACs are recommended over warfarin except in moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis and mechanical valves.

title: Endocarditis antibiotics wait for cultures if the patient can wait
lead: In a stable patient with suspected endocarditis, draw the blood cultures before the antibiotic.
lines: Three sets from separate sticks are the usual ask.
An unstable patient gets the drug after whatever cultures you can draw immediately.
A dental procedure prophylaxis is for a short list of heart lesions, not for every murmur.
miss: Giving one dose of an oral antibiotic and then trying to culture the blood the next day.

source.name: StatPearls. Infective Endocarditis.
source.says: Blood cultures before antibiotics are required for the diagnosis when the patient is stable. Unstable patients are treated immediately after cultures are drawn.

title: Type A dissection is an operation
lead: A dissection that involves the ascending aorta goes to surgery. Blood pressure is lowered with a beta blocker first so the shear falls.
lines: A pure vasodilator first can raise the force of contraction. The beta blocker comes before or with it.
Unequal pulses are the bedside clue you already have.
Thrombolysis is contraindicated.
miss: Starting nicardipine alone, or giving a fibrinolytic for the chest pain.

source.name: StatPearls. Aortic Dissection.
source.says: Ascending involvement is surgical. Heart-rate control precedes pure vasodilation so the force on the flap does not rise.

title: A rupturing aneurysm does not go to the clinic
lead: Hypotension, back or abdominal pain, and a known or pulsatile aneurysm is rupture. The patient goes to repair, not to a repeat ultrasound.
lines: Permissive hypotension is a conversation. Large-volume crystalloid before control can worsen bleeding.
A stable, incidentally found aneurysm is a size and a risk discussion, not an emergency.
Smoking cessation is the medical therapy that changes growth.
miss: Sending the hypotensive patient for a clinic ultrasound this week.

source.name: StatPearls. Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
source.says: Rupture is diagnosed clinically and repaired. Elective repair is a separate decision based on size and risk.

title: Tamponade is drained, not diuresed
lead: Tamponade is treated by removing the pericardial fluid. A diuretic reduces the preload the heart still needed.
lines: Fluids are a bridge while the needle or the window is arranged.
Pulsus paradoxus and equalization are the clues.
A small effusion without equalization is not tamponade and does not need an emergency window.
miss: Giving furosemide for the distended neck veins.

source.name: StatPearls. Cardiac Tamponade.
source.says: Drainage is the treatment. Diuresis reduces filling pressure and can precipitate collapse.

title: Torsades gets magnesium, and the QT drug stops
lead: Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium and by stopping the QT-prolonging drug. A stable patient is not given another QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic.
lines: Correct potassium.
Unstable polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is defibrillated.
A congenital long QT with syncope is a specialist and often a defibrillator conversation, not a higher dose of the offending antibiotic.
miss: Giving amiodarone for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in a patient whose QT is already long.

source.name: StatPearls. Long QT Syndrome.
source.says: Magnesium is first-line for torsades. Offending QT-prolonging drugs are stopped, and potassium is repleted.

title: Typical flutter can be ablated at the isthmus
lead: Typical atrial flutter is treated by ablating the cavotricuspid isthmus when the patient is a candidate. Rate and stroke prevention still matter today.
lines: A ventricular rate of 150 with sawtooth waves is flutter until proved otherwise.
Anticoagulation follows stroke risk, as in fibrillation.
Adenosine may show the flutter waves. It does not cure the circuit.
miss: Cardioverting and stopping anticoagulation because the ECG is now sinus.

source.name: StatPearls. Electrophysiology Study and Ablation of Atrial Flutter.
source.says: Isthmus ablation treats typical flutter. Stroke prevention is based on risk and is not cancelled by sinus rhythm.

title: HFpEF still gets an SGLT2 inhibitor conversation
lead: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is treated for congestion and for the comorbidities. An SGLT2 inhibitor is the drug class with a recommendation, not a loop diuretic alone forever.
lines: The 2022 guideline gives SGLT2 inhibitors a class 2a recommendation in HFpEF.
Blood pressure control is part of the disease, using the current hypertension goal.
Do not apply the four-pillar HFrEF list unchanged and add a beta blocker that the patient does not otherwise need.
miss: Stopping all heart-failure drugs because the ejection fraction is 60% while the patient is still admitted for congestion.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: SGLT2 inhibitors have a recommendation in HFpEF. Congestion is treated, and the HFrEF four-drug list is not copied blindly.

title: Rheumatic fever prevention is penicillin, not a one-time antibiotic
lead: After rheumatic fever, secondary prevention is scheduled penicillin. Treating one sore throat does not finish the job.
lines: The duration depends on whether the heart was involved and on how long ago the attack was.
A new pharyngitis is still treated. Prevention is in addition.
The mitral valve is what you listen to for the rest of the patient's life.
miss: Giving a single course of amoxicillin and discharging the prevention plan.

source.name: StatPearls. Rheumatic Heart Disease.
source.says: Secondary antibiotic prophylaxis prevents recurrent rheumatic fever. One acute course is not prophylaxis.

title: A tet spell is calmed, and the resistance is raised
lead: A hypercyanotic spell in tetralogy is treated by calming the child, giving oxygen, and raising systemic resistance, including knees-to-chest.
lines: A vasoconstrictor is the drug version of squatting when the spell continues.
A drug that drops afterload makes the right-to-left shunt worse.
The murmur getting softer means less blood is crossing the pulmonary valve.
miss: Giving a pure vasodilator during a spell.

source.name: StatPearls. Tetralogy of Fallot.
source.says: Knee-chest position and measures that raise systemic vascular resistance reduce right-to-left shunting during a spell.

title: GOLD group E is one exacerbation
lead: In GOLD 2026, one moderate or severe exacerbation in the past year is group E. Start a LABA plus a LAMA, not a LABA plus an inhaled steroid alone.
lines: Group A has no such exacerbation and few symptoms: a bronchodilator.
Group B has no such exacerbation and more symptoms: LABA plus LAMA.
Add the inhaled steroid as triple therapy when blood eosinophils are at least 300 cells per microliter. Do not start an ICS/LABA pair for COPD without asthma.
miss: Using the old rule that one exacerbation was not enough to leave group A, and starting an ICS/LABA.
diagramAlt: GOLD 2026 groups. No exacerbation and few symptoms: bronchodilator. No exacerbation and more symptoms: LABA plus LAMA. One or more moderate or severe exacerbations: LABA plus LAMA, and consider triple therapy if eosinophils are at least 300.

source.name: GOLD 2026 Report. Key changes.
source.says: One moderate or severe exacerbation now places a treatment-naive patient in group E. Initial therapy for group E is LABA/LAMA, with triple therapy considered at eosinophils of at least 300.

title: No SABA-only asthma plan
lead: Every adolescent and adult with asthma gets an inhaled corticosteroid. As-needed albuterol alone is not a plan.
lines: GINA track 1 uses ICS-formoterol as the reliever at every step.
Steps 1 and 2 are as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol. From step 3 it is also the daily maintenance inhaler.
A short course of systemic steroid treats a severe flare. It is not controller therapy.
miss: Refilling albuterol for daily symptoms and calling the asthma mild.

source.name: 2026 GINA Strategy Report.
source.says: GINA recommends against SABA-only treatment. ICS-formoterol is the preferred anti-inflammatory reliever and reduces severe exacerbations compared with SABA-based care.

title: Where to treat community pneumonia
lead: The first pneumonia decision is the site of care, using severity, not a single lab. Anaerobic coverage is not routine for aspiration.
lines: Healthy outpatients: amoxicillin or doxycycline. A macrolide only where pneumococcal resistance is under 25%.
Comorbid outpatients: a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or doxycycline, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.
Nonsevere inpatient: beta-lactam plus macrolide, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone. Severe: a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a beta-lactam plus a fluoroquinolone.
miss: Adding metronidazole because the word aspiration appeared, or admitting a low-risk patient for an IV drug that an oral regimen covers.

source.name: 2019 IDSA/ATS Guideline for Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Site of care is based on severity. Regimens are split by comorbidity and by ward versus ICU. Routine anaerobic coverage for suspected aspiration is not recommended.

title: Who with a pulmonary embolus gets a lytic
lead: Systemic thrombolysis is for high-risk pulmonary embolism with hypotension or shock. A stable patient is anticoagulated and risk-stratified.
lines: Start anticoagulation when the probability is high and bleeding risk is not prohibitive, even before the confirmatory scan, if the scan will be delayed.
A DOAC is appropriate for most stable patients. Thrombolysis is not.
Right-heart strain with a normal blood pressure is intermediate risk. It is not an automatic lytic.
miss: Giving a lytic because the CT said massive clot, while the blood pressure is normal.

source.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
source.says: Hemodynamic instability defines high-risk pulmonary embolism and is the setting for reperfusion. Stable patients are anticoagulated.

title: Do not stop the SGLT2 inhibitor for the early dip
lead: Start an SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes and CKD when eGFR is at least 20, and for CKD with heart failure or with albuminuria at least 200 mg/g.
lines: The early eGFR dip is hemodynamic. It is not a reason to stop.
Continue the drug if eGFR later falls below 20, unless it is not tolerated or dialysis starts.
Hold it for prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical illness, because of ketosis.
miss: Stopping the drug at the two-week lab because eGFR fell from 48 to 42.

source.name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD.
source.says: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for type 2 diabetes with CKD and eGFR at least 20, and for CKD with albuminuria at least 200 mg/g or with heart failure. The early dip is not an indication to stop.

title: Group A COPD is a bronchodilator, not an inhaled steroid
lead: GOLD 2026 group A, no exacerbation and few symptoms, starts a bronchodilator. An inhaled steroid is not the opening drug.
lines: Group B, symptomatic and no exacerbation, starts LABA plus LAMA.
Group E is one moderate or severe exacerbation and also starts LABA plus LAMA.
Triple therapy is the eosinophil decision, not the default.
miss: Starting every smoker on an ICS/LABA inhaler.

source.name: GOLD 2026 Report. Key changes.
source.says: Initial therapy is a bronchodilator for group A and dual long-acting bronchodilation for groups B and E.

title: A COPD exacerbation gets a steroid, and antibiotics are selective
lead: A COPD exacerbation is treated with a short systemic steroid. Antibiotics are for increased sputum purulence plus increased dyspnea or volume.
lines: Noninvasive ventilation is for respiratory acidosis, not for every wheeze.
Oxygen is titrated. A high flow that abolishes the drive is the old harm.
The maintenance inhalers are restarted or started before discharge.
miss: Giving a 14-day antibiotic to every patient who is a little more short of breath.

source.name: GOLD 2026 Report. Key changes.
source.says: Systemic corticosteroids treat the exacerbation. Antibiotics are added when purulence accompanies more dyspnea or sputum volume.

title: Asthma oxygen starts below 92% and stops by 95%
lead: GINA 2026 does not give oxygen to an adult or adolescent with acute asthma unless the saturation is below 92%. If oxygen is given, the target stays at or under 95%.
lines: The reliever in the preferred track is ICS-formoterol, including during a mild flare.
A systemic steroid is for the severe attack, not for every cough.
Epinephrine is for anaphylaxis, not for ordinary asthma.
miss: Putting a nonrebreather on a talking patient whose saturation is 96%.

source.name: 2026 GINA Strategy Report.
source.says: Supplemental oxygen is reserved for saturation below 92%, with an upper target of 95% in adults and adolescents.

title: Severe pneumonia uses a beta-lactam plus a macrolide
lead: Severe community-acquired pneumonia is treated with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a beta-lactam plus a fluoroquinolone. One drug is not enough.
lines: Nonsevere inpatient pneumonia can be a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.
Add MRSA or Pseudomonas coverage only when the risk the guideline names is present.
Blood cultures are for severe disease, not for every walking outpatient.
miss: Using an oral macrolide alone for a patient who is in shock.

source.name: 2019 IDSA/ATS Guideline for Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Severe pneumonia is combination therapy. MRSA and Pseudomonas coverage is added only for specific risks.

title: A stable pulmonary embolus is anticoagulated
lead: A pulmonary embolus with a normal blood pressure is treated with anticoagulation. Systemic thrombolysis is for hypotension or shock.
lines: Start the anticoagulant if the scan will be delayed and the bleeding risk is acceptable.
Right-heart strain with a normal pressure is not an automatic lytic.
A DOAC is appropriate for most stable patients.
miss: Thrombolysing a clot because the CT report said the clot was large.

source.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
source.says: Hemodynamic instability defines high-risk pulmonary embolism and the reperfusion decision. Stable patients are anticoagulated.

title: Hold the SGLT2 inhibitor when the patient is fasting or critically ill
lead: An SGLT2 inhibitor is held for prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical illness because of ketoacidosis. A small early drop in eGFR is not a reason to stop it forever.
lines: Continue it if the eGFR later falls below 20, unless dialysis starts or the patient cannot tolerate it.
The indication includes type 2 diabetes with CKD and eGFR at least 20, and CKD with heart failure or heavy albuminuria.
Restart it when the patient is eating and stable.
miss: Stopping the drug permanently because eGFR fell 4 points in the first month.

source.name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD.
source.says: The early eGFR dip is not an indication to discontinue. The drug is held during prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical illness.

title: Severe symptoms of hyponatremia get hypertonic saline
lead: A seizure or deep coma from hyponatremia is treated with hypertonic saline now. Fluid restriction is for the stable patient.
lines: The correction over the first day is limited, because a fast rise can injure the myelin.
Recheck the sodium after the bolus. Do not write a large bag and walk away.
SIADH will not be fixed by a liter of normal saline.
miss: Fluid-restricting a seizing patient, or correcting a chronic sodium of 112 up to 140 in one shift.

source.name: StatPearls. Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion.
source.says: Severe neurologic symptoms are treated with hypertonic saline. The daily rise is limited to avoid osmotic demyelination.

title: Central diabetes insipidus answers to desmopressin
lead: If desmopressin concentrates the urine, the diabetes insipidus is central and desmopressin is the treatment. If it does not, the kidney is the problem.
lines: Nephrogenic disease from lithium is not fixed by more desmopressin.
The patient must be allowed to drink, or you replace the water.
A low sodium means you gave too much desmopressin or the patient drank past it.
miss: Restricting free water in a hypernatremic patient whose urine is already water.

source.name: StatPearls. Arginine Vasopressin Disorder (Diabetes Insipidus).
source.says: A response to desmopressin defines central diabetes insipidus and is the basis of replacement. Nephrogenic disease does not respond.

title: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis is the hyperkalemic one
lead: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis raises potassium. It is low aldosterone effect, often from diabetes or from a drug that blocks that axis.
lines: Stop the offending drug when you can: a potassium-sparing diuretic, an NSAID, or sometimes the ACE inhibitor if the potassium is dangerous.
Type 1 and type 2 waste potassium. Do not treat them as type 4.
Fludrocortisone is a selected treatment, not the first reflex.
miss: Giving more spironolactone for the blood pressure while the potassium is 6.2.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Tubular Acidosis.
source.says: Type 4 is hyperkalemic acidosis from aldosterone deficiency or resistance. The other renal tubular acidoses are hypokalemic.

title: Saline-responsive alkalosis gets chloride
lead: A metabolic alkalosis with a low urine chloride is treated with saline and potassium. A high urine chloride is mineralocorticoid excess and saline will not fix it.
lines: Vomiting and a remote diuretic are the low-chloride stories.
Active diuretic use can look high-chloride. The history matters.
Acetazolamide is a selected option when the patient cannot take volume, not the first bag.
miss: Pouring saline into primary hyperaldosteronism.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Metabolic Alkalosis.
source.says: Urine chloride separates saline-responsive alkalosis from saline-unresponsive mineralocorticoid excess.

title: Ventilate the patient whose CO2 is rising
lead: A rising PaCO2 with a falling pH is treated by ventilation. Oxygen does not remove CO2.
lines: Noninvasive ventilation is the first step when the patient can protect the airway and is not in shock.
A chronic retainer is not driven to a CO2 of 40 in an hour.
Sedation that is still running is a cause you can stop.
miss: Increasing the oxygen liter flow as the only response to a CO2 of 80 and a pH of 7.18.

source.name: StatPearls. Respiratory Acidosis.
source.says: Hypoventilation is treated by increasing alveolar ventilation. Oxygen does not correct the carbon dioxide.

title: Tension pneumothorax is decompressed before the film
lead: A hypotensive patient with a shifted trachea and absent breath sounds is decompressed. The chest film is for the patient who can wait.
lines: Needle or finger decompression is followed by a chest tube.
The trachea moves away from the side of the tension.
A simple pneumothorax in a stable patient can wait for the image.
miss: Sending a crashing patient to radiology for a two-view film.

source.name: StatPearls. Tension Pneumothorax.
source.says: Clinical tension pneumothorax is decompressed immediately. Imaging is reserved for stable patients.

title: ARDS tidal volume is predicted body weight
lead: Ventilate the acute respiratory distress syndrome at about 6 mL per kilogram of predicted body weight, and keep the plateau pressure at or under 30.
lines: Predicted weight comes from height and sex, not from the scale.
Chasing a normal CO2 with big breaths injures the lung.
Fluids are conservative once shock has been resuscitated.
miss: Setting 12 mL per kilogram of actual weight because the saturation looks better.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
source.says: Low tidal volume on predicted body weight and a plateau-pressure limit are the ventilator settings that reduce further lung injury.

title: Remove the antigen in hypersensitivity pneumonitis
lead: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is treated by removing the bird, the mold, or the farm antigen. A steroid without removal fails.
lines: The history is the test you cannot order.
Acute disease follows exposure by hours.
Chronic scarring will not reverse if the patient goes home to the same bird.
miss: Adding a steroid and sending the patient back to the pigeon coop.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
source.says: Antigen removal is required. Corticosteroids do not substitute for it.

title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is not a prednisone disease
lead: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is treated with an antifibrotic drug and supportive care, not with a long prednisone course as the disease-modifying plan.
lines: Oxygen for hypoxemia and pulmonary rehabilitation are part of care.
A connective-tissue disease or an exposure has to be excluded first.
Acute worsening is a different event and needs a different evaluation.
miss: Prescribing months of high-dose prednisone as the only treatment of honeycombing.

source.name: StatPearls. Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
source.says: Antifibrotic therapy is the disease-specific treatment. Long-term corticosteroids are not disease-modifying for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Bronchiectasis is cleared, and antibiotics treat the flare
lead: Bronchiectasis is treated with airway clearance every day. Antibiotics treat a flare or a identified organism such as Pseudomonas, not the anatomy.
lines: Find the cause: cystic fibrosis, immunodeficiency, or a prior infection.
A CT that shows the dilation is the diagnosis. A normal film does not exclude it.
Suppressive antibiotics are a specialist decision, not the first inhaler.
miss: Rotating oral antibiotics forever and never teaching clearance.

source.name: StatPearls. Bronchiectasis.
source.says: Daily airway clearance is the foundation. Antibiotics treat exacerbations and specific chronic infections.

title: Correct hypernatremia slowly
lead: Replace the free-water deficit of hypernatremia gradually. A fast drop swells a brain that has made new osmoles.
lines: The urine tells you if the kidney is holding water.
Let a patient with an intact thirst drink.
Desmopressin is for central diabetes insipidus, not for a patient who simply had no access to water.
miss: Dropping the sodium from 162 to 140 overnight with free water.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypernatremia.
source.says: The water deficit is replaced slowly to avoid cerebral edema. The cause, intake versus renal loss, decides the drug.

title: Do not push potassium
lead: Intravenous potassium is diluted and infused. It is never pushed. Magnesium is replaced when the potassium will not stay up.
lines: Oral replacement is safer when the patient can take it and the ECG is quiet.
ECG changes or severe weakness justify the intravenous route, still controlled.
A diuretic cause means you also change the diuretic.
miss: Injecting a syringe of concentrated potassium.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypokalemia.
source.says: Intravenous potassium is infused, never pushed. Magnesium deficiency is corrected or the potassium loss continues.

title: Symptomatic hypocalcemia gets calcium
lead: A seizure, tetany, or a long QT from hypocalcemia gets intravenous calcium. Asymptomatic mild hypocalcemia is oral and a search for the cause.
lines: Check magnesium. A low magnesium keeps calcium low.
After thyroid surgery, watch the calcium for the first day.
Correct the albumin before you call a total calcium low.
miss: Giving a bolus of calcium for a mildly low total calcium in a comfortable patient with a low albumin.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypocalcemia.
source.says: Intravenous calcium is for severe or symptomatic hypocalcemia. Magnesium is checked because it impairs parathyroid hormone release.

title: Adult polycystic kidney disease: treat the pressure and the headache
lead: Hypertension in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is treated. A sudden severe headache is an aneurysm until imaged.
lines: The kidneys are not biopsied to make this diagnosis.
Tolvaptan is a selected drug that slows growth in the right patient, with a liver-test cost.
Family screening is a conversation, not a surprise CT of every relative.
miss: Ignoring a thunderclap headache because the patient's usual problem is the kidney.

source.name: StatPearls. Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
source.says: Hypertension is treated early. Sudden headache raises concern for aneurysm. Diagnosis is imaging and family history, not biopsy.

title: Alkalinize a uric acid stone
lead: Uric acid stones dissolve when the urine is made less acidic. A plain film that is clear does not mean the stone is gone.
lines: CT or ultrasound sees the stone the film missed.
Allopurinol is for the uric acid production, not the acute colic.
Pain control and a strainer still happen.
miss: Telling the patient the stone passed because the abdominal film is blank.

source.name: StatPearls. Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis.
source.says: Urine alkalinization dissolves uric acid stones. They are radiolucent on plain radiographs.

title: Bind phosphate with the meal
lead: A phosphate binder is taken with food. A binder swallowed on an empty stomach does not bind the meal the patient is about to eat.
lines: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is treated by lowering phosphate and replacing the vitamin D the kidney no longer activates, in the order the labs demand.
Calcium-based binders add a calcium load. Watch the product.
Dialysis does not excuse the binder.
miss: Prescribing the binder at bedtime, away from meals.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD).
source.says: Phosphate binders work when they meet dietary phosphate. Timing with meals is the instruction.

title: A young woman with fibromuscular stenosis may benefit from opening the artery
lead: Fibromuscular dysplasia of a renal artery in a young woman is the stenosis that is often opened. An older atherosclerotic stenosis is not automatically stented.
lines: An ACE inhibitor can drop the filtration when the whole renal mass sits behind a stenosis.
Recheck the creatinine after you start it.
A bruit is a clue, not a diagnosis.
miss: Stenting every atherosclerotic renal artery because the pressure is high.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Artery Stenosis.
source.says: Revascularization is most clearly useful in fibromuscular dysplasia. Atherosclerotic disease is not stented by reflex.

title: Gas in a diabetic kidney is not oral antibiotics
lead: Emphysematous pyelonephritis is treated with antibiotics and a plan to drain or remove the source. It is not a three-day outpatient prescription.
lines: The patient is usually diabetic.
Imaging shows the gas.
A simple pyelonephritis has no gas and can be outpatient if the patient can drink and is not septic.
miss: Discharging a febrile diabetic with gas around the kidney on ciprofloxacin.

source.name: StatPearls. Emphysematous Pyelonephritis.
source.says: Gas-forming kidney infection requires intravenous antibiotics and source control, not oral therapy alone.

title: Minimal change disease in a child is a steroid trial
lead: A child with sudden nephrotic syndrome is treated as minimal change disease with steroids unless a red flag demands a biopsy first.
lines: Hematuria that is heavy, a low complement, or an age outside childhood are reasons not to assume it.
The parents are taught to check the urine and the swelling.
Relapse is common and is not failure of the diagnosis.
miss: Biopsying every edematous toddler before a pediatric nephrologist has seen them.

source.name: StatPearls. Minimal Change Disease.
source.says: Typical childhood nephrotic syndrome is treated as steroid-sensitive minimal change disease unless atypical features require a biopsy.

title: Membranous nephropathy: look for the cause and the clot
lead: Adult membranous nephropathy is tested for PLA2R antibody, hepatitis, lupus, and cancer, and the nephrotic syndrome is a clot risk.
lines: Anticoagulation is considered when the albumin is very low and the bleeding risk allows it.
Not every patient needs immediate immunosuppression.
A renal-vein thrombosis is flank pain and a worsening kidney, not just more protein.
miss: Starting high-dose steroids on day one and never testing for hepatitis B.

source.name: StatPearls. Membranous Nephropathy.
source.says: Secondary causes are excluded, PLA2R marks primary disease, and heavy proteinuria creates a thrombosis risk.

title: Resuscitate the bleed, then scope it
lead: For a stable ulcer bleed without cardiovascular disease, transfuse at a hemoglobin of 7. Scope after resuscitation, within 24 hours.
lines: Two large IVs, a type and screen, and a restrictive transfusion strategy come before the endoscopy.
High-risk stigmata get endoscopic therapy and a proton-pump inhibitor infusion.
A higher transfusion threshold is reasonable for active cardiovascular disease. The number 7 is not universal.
miss: Transfusing to a hemoglobin of 10 before the scope, or scoping an unstable patient.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Upper Gastrointestinal and Ulcer Bleeding.
source.says: A restrictive threshold of 7 g/dL is recommended for patients without cardiovascular disease. Endoscopy follows resuscitation, generally within 24 hours.

title: Tap the new ascites
lead: New ascites gets a diagnostic tap. A SAAG of 1.1 or more means portal hypertension. A neutrophil count of 250 or more means spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
lines: Send the cell count, albumin, protein, and culture inoculated at the bedside.
Do not wait for the culture to start antibiotics when the neutrophil count is already at least 250.
For a tap that removes more than 5 liters, give albumin, about 6 to 8 g per liter removed.
miss: Sending the patient home on a higher diuretic dose without tapping new or painful ascites.

source.name: StatPearls. Ascites. AASLD practice guidance on ascites and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
source.says: Diagnostic paracentesis defines the fluid. SAAG at or above 1.1 supports portal hypertension. Neutrophils at or above 250 define spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Large-volume removal is paired with albumin.

title: The two ulcer causes are H. pylori and NSAIDs
lead: A peptic ulcer is Helicobacter pylori or an NSAID until a rarer cause is proved. The pain’s relation to meals is not reliable enough to locate it.
lines: A clean-based ulcer that has stopped bleeding does not need a heroic transfusion target.
Alarm features, including bleeding, weight loss, and age, get an endoscopy.
Stop the NSAID. Treat the infection. A proton-pump inhibitor covers the healing.
miss: Locating the ulcer from whether food helps, and never testing for H. pylori.

source.name: StatPearls. Peptic Ulcer Disease.
source.says: H. pylori and NSAIDs cause most peptic ulcers. Endoscopy is for alarm features and for bleeding, not for every episode of dyspepsia.

title: Reflux is a sphincter that relaxes, not a weak swallow
lead: Gastroesophageal reflux is transient relaxation of the lower sphincter. Dysphagia, bleeding, or weight loss is an alarm, not simple reflux.
lines: A trial of acid suppression is reasonable when the story is heartburn and there is no alarm.
An alarm symptom gets an endoscopy, not a longer antacid trial.
Weight loss and a head of the bed are part of the treatment, not decorations.
miss: Refilling a proton-pump inhibitor for progressive dysphagia.

source.name: StatPearls. Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
source.says: Transient lower-sphincter relaxation is the mechanism. Alarm symptoms move the patient to endoscopy.

title: Pancreatitis is lipase, gallstones, and alcohol
lead: Acute pancreatitis is epigastric pain to the back with a lipase at least three times normal. Gallstones and alcohol are the two causes to name first.
lines: Amylase is less specific. Lipase is the enzyme.
Fluids are the early treatment. A meal returns when the pain allows. Prolonged fasting is not the plan.
A rising hematocrit and a rising urea mark a patient who is under-resuscitated.
miss: Starving the patient for a week because the lipase was high on day one.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Pancreatitis.
source.says: The diagnosis is characteristic pain plus lipase. Gallstones and alcohol lead the cause list, and early feeding replaces prolonged fasting.

title: Small-bowel obstruction stacks air-fluid levels
lead: Small-bowel obstruction is vomiting, distension, and air-fluid levels. Prior surgery means adhesions until a hernia or a mass is found.
lines: A closed loop and a fever or a lactate that is rising is ischemia. That patient does not wait.
Nasogastric suction and fluids are the first orders for a stable partial obstruction.
Complete obstruction with peritonitis is an operation.
miss: Watching a febrile, acidotic obstruction overnight because the last one was adhesions.

source.name: StatPearls. Small Bowel Obstruction.
source.says: Adhesions are the common cause after surgery. Peritonitis, fever, or a rising lactate marks ischemia and changes the plan to the operating room.

title: Mesenteric ischemia hurts more than the exam shows
lead: Acute mesenteric ischemia is pain out of proportion to the exam. Atrial fibrillation or a low-flow state is the setup, and lactate is late.
lines: The embolus prefers the superior mesenteric artery.
A soft abdomen does not reassure you. The abdomen becomes hard when the bowel is already dead.
CT angiography is the test. A plain film is not.
miss: Waiting for the lactate or the rigid abdomen before calling the surgeon.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.
source.says: Pain out of proportion with a cardiac source is mesenteric ischemia until angiography says otherwise. Lactate rises after the bowel is injured.

title: Cholecystitis is a blocked cystic duct
lead: Acute cholecystitis is a stone blocking the cystic duct. The pain is right-upper-quadrant and Murphy's sign stops the breath.
lines: Fever and a high white count mark inflammation, not just biliary colic.
Ultrasound shows the wall, the stone, and the fluid.
Early surgery is the treatment of uncomplicated disease. Antibiotics alone do not remove the stone.
miss: Diagnosing cholangitis, which adds jaundice and needs a drained duct, from an isolated gallbladder.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.
source.says: Cystic-duct obstruction produces gallbladder-wall inflammation. Early cholecystectomy is the definitive treatment.

title: Achalasia is opened or injected, not suppressed with acid medicine
