lead: Achalasia is treated by disrupting the lower sphincter: dilation, surgery, or an endoscopic myotomy. A proton-pump inhibitor does not relax it.
lines: Manometry confirms the diagnosis.
Endoscopy excludes a cancer at the junction that mimics the beak.
Aspiration at night is why the treatment is not optional.
miss: Refilling a proton-pump inhibitor for regurgitation of undigested food.

source.name: StatPearls. Achalasia.
source.says: LES disruption is the treatment. Acid suppression does not restore relaxation or peristalsis.

title: Celiac disease is a gluten-free diet, after the test
lead: Celiac disease is treated by removing gluten. Do the serology and, when needed, the biopsy before the diet, or the tests go negative.
lines: Check total IgA or the test lies.
Dermatitis herpetiformis is the same diet.
A first-degree relative with symptoms is tested. A gene test alone is not the diagnosis.
miss: Starting a gluten-free diet the week before the endoscopy.

source.name: StatPearls. Celiac Disease.
source.says: The gluten-free diet is the treatment and is started after serology or biopsy, because the diet heals the test.

title: Severe ulcerative colitis is admitted, and antidiarrheals stop
lead: Severe ulcerative colitis is admitted for steroids and for a watch on toxic megacolon. Antidiarrheals and opioids are stopped.
lines: Stool studies exclude infection, including C. difficile, before you blame the disease alone.
A toxic, dilated colon is a surgical conversation.
Long-standing disease gets cancer surveillance. A flare visit is not that colonoscopy.
miss: Sending a patient with ten bloody stools a day and a fever home on loperamide.

source.name: StatPearls. Ulcerative Colitis.
source.says: Severe colitis is treated in the hospital. Antimotility drugs are avoided because they precipitate toxic megacolon.

title: Chronic pancreatitis enzymes are taken with the meal
lead: Pancreatic enzymes are swallowed with food. A capsule at bedtime does not treat the steatorrhea of the meal.
lines: Diabetes from lost islets is treated as diabetes.
Alcohol is stopped. That is the disease-modifying act.
A new jaundice is cancer until imaged, not more enzymes.
miss: Prescribing the enzymes once daily on an empty stomach.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Pancreatitis.
source.says: Enzyme replacement is taken with meals. Alcohol cessation is required. New biliary obstruction is investigated as cancer.

title: Varices bleed: drug, antibiotic, band
lead: Suspected variceal bleeding gets a vasoactive drug such as octreotide, an intravenous antibiotic, and urgent endoscopy for banding.
lines: Resuscitate, but do not flood the patient into a higher portal pressure.
A nonselective beta blocker is secondary prevention after the bleeding stops, not a drug for the shock bay.
Intubation for a massive hematemesis protects the airway before the scope.
miss: Starting propranolol while the pressure is 80 and the patient is still vomiting blood.

source.name: StatPearls. Esophageal Varices.
source.says: Vasoactive therapy, antibiotics, and endoscopic banding treat acute variceal bleeding. Beta blockers are for after hemostasis.

title: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy starts at 140/90
lead: Treat chronic hypertension in pregnancy at 140/90. Do not wait for 160/110.
lines: This is the CHAP threshold ACOG adopted. It is a threshold to treat, not a proved ideal target below 140/90.
Continue an effective agent that is safe in pregnancy. Labetalol, nifedipine, and hydralazine are the usual choices.
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and a statin stay stopped.
miss: Stopping the patient's amlodipine-class plan and watching until the pressure is severe. The error is the wait, and also keeping an ACE inhibitor.

source.name: ACOG Practice Advisory. Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP).
source.says: ACOG recommends 140/90 mm Hg as the threshold to start or titrate treatment for chronic hypertension in pregnancy.

title: Severe hypertension in pregnancy is treated now
lead: A sustained pressure of 160 systolic or 110 diastolic in pregnancy or postpartum is treated promptly. Magnesium is for the seizure risk, not for the pressure.
lines: Confirm a severe value and treat. Do not wait four hours, and do not wait for the labs.
IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate-release oral nifedipine are the acute drugs.
Magnesium sulfate prevents the seizure. It is given with the antihypertensive, not instead of it.
miss: Starting magnesium and leaving a pressure of 180/115 untreated while the labs are pending.

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia.
source.says: Severe-range blood pressure is treated urgently. Magnesium sulfate is seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia with severe features.

title: Who gets aspirin to prevent preeclampsia
lead: High-risk patients start low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks to lower the risk of preeclampsia.
lines: High risk includes prior preeclampsia, a multifetal pregnancy, chronic hypertension, diabetes, kidney disease, and autoimmune disease.
The dose used in the recommendation is 81 mg daily.
Aspirin does not treat severe-range pressures that are already present.
miss: Saving the aspirin for the third trimester, or offering it as the treatment of a pressure of 170/110.

source.name: USPSTF. Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality.
source.says: Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks is recommended for pregnant people at high risk of preeclampsia.

title: Give insulin in DKA until the gap closes
lead: In diabetic ketoacidosis, continue insulin after the glucose falls and add dextrose. Stop insulin when the gap has closed and the patient is eating, not when the glucose first looks pretty.
lines: If potassium is under 3.3, replace it before insulin.
The 2024 hyperglycemic-crisis guidance is fluids, potassium, and insulin, and bicarbonate is not routine.
An SGLT2 inhibitor can cause ketoacidosis with a glucose that is not very high. Ask about the drug.
miss: Turning off the insulin drip because the glucose reached 180 while the bicarbonate is still 10.

source.name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
source.says: Insulin continues until ketoacidosis resolves. Dextrose is added when glucose falls so the insulin can keep running.

title: Thyroid storm: block, then iodine
lead: In thyroid storm give a beta blocker and a thionamide before iodine. Iodine first supplies substrate for more hormone.
lines: A glucocorticoid is part of the regimen.
Treat the trigger.
Do not use aspirin for the fever.
miss: Giving potassium iodide in the ambulance before any thionamide.

source.name: StatPearls. Thyroid Storm.
source.says: The thionamide precedes iodine. Beta blockade and a glucocorticoid are given, and the precipitant is treated.

title: Adrenal crisis is steroid and saline, before the stim test
lead: Adrenal crisis is hydrocortisone and saline now. A cosyntropin test can wait until the patient is alive.
lines: Primary disease is hyperkalemic and dark. Do not wait for that classic picture if the patient is in shock and on chronic steroids.
A patient who takes prednisone every day and then vomits needs a stress dose.
Antibiotics for sepsis are added when sepsis is the trigger. They do not replace the steroid.
miss: Waiting for a morning cortisol while the pressure is 70.

source.name: StatPearls. Adrenal Insufficiency.
source.says: Stress-dose glucocorticoid and intravenous saline are given immediately. Diagnostic testing is deferred.

title: Block alpha before beta in a pheochromocytoma
lead: Prepare a pheochromocytoma with an alpha blocker until the patient is volume-replete, and only then add a beta blocker.
lines: The test is metanephrines, drawn correctly.
Surgery is after the block, not before.
A beta blocker first can raise the pressure.
miss: Starting metoprolol for the palpitations the day the CT shows an adrenal mass.

source.name: StatPearls. Pheochromocytoma.
source.says: Alpha blockade and volume replacement precede beta blockade and precede resection.

title: Pick the diabetes drug for the disease, not the A1C
lead: In type 2 diabetes, start an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven benefit for heart failure, kidney disease, or atherosclerotic disease even when the A1C is already at goal.
lines: Heart failure gets an SGLT2 inhibitor.
Atherosclerotic disease can get a GLP-1 receptor agonist, an SGLT2 inhibitor, or both.
Do not wait through a failed metformin trial when one of those diseases is already present.
miss: Withholding the drug because the A1C is 6.8.

source.name: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment.
source.says: Agents with proven cardiovascular or kidney benefit are recommended irrespective of A1C when heart failure, chronic kidney disease, or atherosclerotic disease is present.

title: A prolactinoma is a dopamine agonist, after the exclusions
lead: Once pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and drugs are excluded, a prolactinoma is treated with a dopamine agonist.
lines: Cabergoline is the usual drug.
A visual-field cut is an urgent MRI and an urgent treatment, not a routine refill.
Surgery is for the patient who cannot take the drug or whose vision is failing despite it.
miss: Booking transsphenoidal surgery before a pregnancy test.

source.name: StatPearls. Prolactinoma.
source.says: Dopamine agonists are first-line after secondary causes are excluded. Surgery is reserved for drug failure or vision that is threatened.

title: Endometriosis pain is suppressed, and a large cyst is not
lead: Endometriosis pain is treated with hormonal suppression. A large endometrioma is a surgical lesion, not a longer oral contraceptive alone.
lines: Infertility is managed with the fertility plan, which may not be the same as the pain plan.
NSAIDs help pain and do not treat the implants.
A normal exam does not end the workup of cyclic pain and infertility.
miss: Telling a patient with a 7-centimeter chocolate cyst to try ibuprofen for a year.

source.name: StatPearls. Endometriosis.
source.says: Hormonal therapy treats pain. Large endometriomas are managed surgically. Infertility care is planned separately.

title: A ruptured ectopic pregnancy is an operation
lead: A patient with a positive pregnancy test, an empty uterus, and shock goes to surgery. Methotrexate is for a stable, selected ectopic pregnancy.
lines: The criteria for methotrexate include a low hCG, no fetal heartbeat, and a patient who can return.
Rh status is checked.
A falling hCG still needs a documented plan.
miss: Giving methotrexate in the emergency department to a dizzy patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Ectopic Pregnancy.
source.says: Rupture is surgical. Methotrexate is limited to hemodynamically stable patients who meet selection criteria.

title: Abruption is resuscitation and delivery decisions, not a cervical check
lead: Placental abruption is maternal resuscitation, a fetal monitor, and a delivery decision. Do not perform a digital exam until previa is excluded.
lines: Blood products are ready because the clotting factors are consumed.
A dead fetus and coagulopathy is an urgent delivery.
Painful bleeding is not previa.
miss: Checking dilation with a finger as the first act.

source.name: StatPearls. Placental Abruption.
source.says: Resuscitation and timely delivery are the treatment. Digital examination is deferred until placenta previa is excluded.

title: Previa is delivered operatively when it covers the cervix
lead: A placenta that covers the cervix is delivered by cesarean. Pelvic rest and a planned date are the outpatient plan after the acute bleed has stopped.
lines: A prior cesarean plus previa raises the chance of placenta accreta. That delivery is planned in a center that can handle it.
The acute bleed is resuscitated like any maternal hemorrhage.
Ultrasound, not a finger, makes the diagnosis.
miss: Inducing labor through a complete previa.

source.name: StatPearls. Placenta Previa.
source.says: Complete previa is delivered by cesarean. Accreta risk rises after prior cesarean and changes where the delivery happens.

title: Gestational diabetes is treated to a tight glucose, and the newborn is watched
lead: Gestational diabetes that is not controlled with diet is treated with insulin. The newborn is watched for hypoglycemia.
lines: The screen is at 24 to 28 weeks unless earlier risk moves it up.
Oral agents are a selected alternative, not a reason to ignore a very high glucose.
The mother is tested for diabetes after the pregnancy.
miss: Reassuring a glucose of 180 after meals because the pregnancy is otherwise normal.

source.name: StatPearls. Gestational Diabetes.
source.says: Insulin is added when diet fails. Neonatal hypoglycemia is anticipated, and the mother is rescreened postpartum.

title: Do not combine a nitrate and a PDE-5 inhibitor
lead: If a patient has taken a PDE-5 inhibitor, do not give nitroglycerin. The pressure can collapse.
lines: Ask the question out loud before the first spray.
The wait after sildenafil is longer than after some newer drugs. If you do not know the interval, do not give the nitrate.
Chest pain still gets an ECG and the rest of the ACS plan that is safe.
miss: Giving the spray because the chest pain protocol says so, without asking.

source.name: StatPearls. Erectile Dysfunction.
source.says: Nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors together cause hypotension and are contraindicated.

title: An alpha blocker works this week. A 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor works in months
lead: For benign prostatic hyperplasia, an alpha blocker relieves symptoms in days. A 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor shrinks the gland over months and is for a large gland.
lines: A post-void residual and a urine culture belong in the visit when infection or retention is possible.
A nodule or a rising PSA is cancer until evaluated.
Red flags of retention, infection, and renal failure are not treated with a tamsulosin sample alone.
miss: Promising a man that finasteride will help him urinate tonight.

source.name: StatPearls. Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
source.says: Alpha blockers are rapid. 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors are for larger glands and take months. Nodules are not dismissed as hyperplasia.

title: Torsion of the testis is detorsed, not imaged to death
lead: A clear testicular torsion goes to the operating room. Ultrasound is for the case that is not clear, and it is not allowed to consume the six-hour window.
lines: The other side is fixed.
Pain relief after manual detorsion does not cancel the operation.
Epididymitis has fever, pyuria, and a present cremasteric reflex.
miss: Booking a Doppler study for the next available slot in the morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Testicular Torsion.
source.says: Immediate surgical exploration is the treatment of a convincing exam. Imaging must not delay it.

title: Ovarian torsion is detorsed even if flow was seen
lead: Ovarian torsion with a convincing story goes to surgery. A Doppler that shows flow does not cancel the operation.
lines: Detorsion and preservation of the ovary is the goal.
A pregnancy test is done because ectopic pregnancy is the other emergency.
Analgesia is given. Observation overnight of a twisting ovary is not.
miss: Discharging the patient because arterial flow was documented.

source.name: StatPearls. Ovarian Torsion.
source.says: Surgery is indicated on clinical grounds. Preserved Doppler flow does not exclude torsion.

title: Pelvic inflammatory disease treats the patient and the partner
lead: Pelvic inflammatory disease is treated with a regimen that covers gonorrhea and chlamydia, and the partner is treated.
lines: A tubo-ovarian abscess that does not improve is drained.
Perihepatitis is the right-upper-quadrant pain. Do not take that patient only to general surgery and forget the pelvis.
A pregnancy test comes first.
miss: Treating the patient with a single dose and not telling the partner.

source.name: StatPearls. Pelvic Inflammatory Disease.
source.says: Empiric coverage includes gonorrhea and chlamydia, partners are treated, and an abscess that fails antibiotics is drained.

title: The sepsis actions, in order
lead: For suspected sepsis, measure lactate, draw cultures if it does not delay the drug, and give a broad antibiotic. Hypotension or a lactate of 4 or more gets crystalloid.
lines: The Surviving Sepsis hour-1 bundle is those actions plus vasopressors during or after fluid if the patient is still hypotensive, aiming for a mean pressure of 65.
The fluid suggestion for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion is at least 30 mL/kg of IV crystalloid, then reassess. It is not an unmeasured bolus.
A virus swab does not replace the antibiotic while bacterial infection is still possible.
miss: Waiting for the lactate to come back before the antibiotic, or giving a liter and walking away.

source.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 Adult Guidelines.
source.says: The hour-1 bundle is lactate, cultures, antibiotics, crystalloid for hypoperfusion, and vasopressors to a mean arterial pressure of 65 when hypotension persists.

title: Epinephrine is the anaphylaxis drug
lead: Anaphylaxis gets intramuscular epinephrine into the mid-outer thigh first. Antihistamines do not treat the airway.
lines: Adult dose: 0.3 to 0.5 mg of 1 mg/mL epinephrine, intramuscularly. Repeat if needed.
The intravenous infusion is for shock that did not respond, not the opening dose.
Observe after the response. A biphasic reaction is why the patient does not leave in ten minutes.
miss: Giving diphenhydramine and a steroid and calling that treatment while the pressure is falling.

source.name: StatPearls. Anaphylaxis.
source.says: Intramuscular epinephrine is first-line. Antihistamines and glucocorticoids do not replace it.

title: Give 100% oxygen for carbon monoxide, and do not trust the pulse oximeter
lead: Carbon monoxide poisoning is treated with 100% oxygen immediately. The pulse oximeter and the PaO2 will look fine.
lines: Hyperbaric oxygen is for loss of consciousness, pregnancy, cardiac ischemia, or a very high level.
The whole household is the exposure. Ask who else was home.
A normal lactate does not clear a fire victim.
miss: Discharging a headache after a heater exposure because the saturation was 99%.

source.name: StatPearls. Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.
source.says: High-flow oxygen is started immediately. Standard oximetry does not detect carboxyhemoglobin.

title: Start N-acetylcysteine for a toxic acetaminophen ingestion
lead: A toxic acetaminophen level, or a staggered ingestion you cannot plot, gets N-acetylcysteine. Do not wait for the ALT to rise.
lines: The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is for one ingestion at a known time.
Charcoal is only if the ingestion was recent and the airway is safe.
Liver failure is a transplant conversation, and the antidote is still given.
miss: Repeating the ALT in the morning before the antidote, in a patient who took the bottle at noon.

source.name: StatPearls. Acetaminophen Toxicity.
source.says: N-acetylcysteine is given for toxic and for high-risk unknown-time ingestions. Enzyme rise lags behind the injury.

title: Naloxone wears off before the opioid does
lead: Naloxone reverses opioid apnea and then wears off. The patient is watched, and the dose is repeated or infused.
lines: The airway is opened first if the patient is not breathing.
A co-ingestant is why some patients do not wake fully.
Do not discharge a long-acting opioid overdose after a single wake-up.
miss: Sending a patient home twenty minutes after one dose of naloxone.

source.name: StatPearls. Opioid Toxicity.
source.says: Naloxone's duration is shorter than many opioids. Recurrence of apnea is expected and is monitored.

title: Do not give flumazenil to a dependent patient
lead: Benzodiazepine overdose is supported at the airway. Flumazenil is avoided when the patient takes the drug every day or has a seizure history, because it can precipitate a seizure.
lines: The dangerous partner is an opioid. Give naloxone for the apnea.
A single naive ingestion in a monitored setting is the rare time flumazenil is discussed.
Withdrawal from a stopped chronic benzodiazepine is treated by reinstating a taper, not by an antidote.
miss: Waking a daily alprazolam user with flumazenil in the hallway.

source.name: StatPearls. Benzodiazepine Toxicity.
source.says: Supportive care is the treatment. Flumazenil is contraindicated in dependent patients because of seizures.

title: Alcohol withdrawal is a benzodiazepine titrated to symptoms
lead: Alcohol withdrawal is treated with a benzodiazepine dosed to the tremor, the vital signs, and the confusion. A protocol that front-loads is safer than chasing the next seizure.
lines: Thiamine is given before glucose.
Delirium tremens is a monitored bed.
An antipsychotic alone does not prevent the seizure.
miss: Giving haloperidol as the only drug for a tremulous, tachycardic patient two days after the last drink.

source.name: StatPearls. Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome.
source.says: Benzodiazepines are titrated to withdrawal severity. Thiamine precedes glucose. Antipsychotics do not treat the withdrawal.

title: Rhabdomyolysis is fluids and a potassium you recheck
lead: Rhabdomyolysis is treated with intravenous fluids. The potassium is rechecked because it can stop the heart before the creatinine rises.
lines: The urine dip lies. Look at the microscope.
A tight limb is a compartment and is opened.
Statins and fibrates together are a cause you stop.
miss: Giving a loop diuretic as the first treatment of tea-colored urine.

source.name: StatPearls. Rhabdomyolysis.
source.says: Volume resuscitation protects the kidney. Hyperkalemia is treated as the immediate threat.

title: Dantrolene is the drug for malignant hyperthermia
lead: Malignant hyperthermia is treated by stopping the volatile anesthetic and giving dantrolene. Cooling and hyperventilation come with it.
lines: The CO2 rises first. The temperature follows.
Call for help and the dantrolene cart. Do not keep the vaporizer on.
It is not treated as ordinary intraoperative fever.
miss: Turning up the volatile agent because the patient looks light.

source.name: StatPearls. Malignant Hyperthermia.
source.says: The triggering anesthetic is stopped and dantrolene is given. Hyperventilation and cooling are supportive.

title: Fat embolism is supported, not anticoagulated as the only plan
lead: Fat embolism syndrome is treated by supporting the lungs and immobilizing the fracture. Heparin is not the specific antidote.
lines: The timing is one to three days after the long-bone injury.
Petechiae on the chest support the diagnosis and are often absent.
A true venous thrombus can coexist. Do not miss it, and do not call every hypoxic fracture patient a clot.
miss: Starting a heparin drip and cancelling the fixation that would stop the embolization.

source.name: StatPearls. Fat Embolism and Fat Embolism Syndrome.
source.says: Supportive care and fracture fixation are the treatment. Anticoagulation is not a specific therapy for fat embolism.

title: The four screens and the ages
lead: Mammography starts at 40 and is every other year through 74. Colorectal screening starts at 45. Lung screening is annual low-dose CT from 50 to 80 after 20 pack-years.
lines: Cervical screening starts at 21. Ages 21 to 29: cytology every 3 years. Ages 30 to 65: cytology every 3 years, high-risk HPV every 5 years, or both every 5 years.
Stop lung screening after 15 years without smoking, or when a comorbidity limits the benefit.
A family history or a prior high-risk lesion changes the colorectal plan. The age-45 start is for average risk.
miss: Starting mammography at 50, or starting colorectal screening at 50, because that was the old age.
diagramAlt: Screening ages. Breast: every other year from 40 through 74. Colon: start at 45. Lung: yearly low-dose CT from 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years. Cervix: start at 21.

source.name: USPSTF recommendations on breast, colorectal, lung, and cervical cancer screening.
source.says: Breast screening is biennial from 40 through 74 (2024). Colorectal screening starts at 45 (2021). Lung screening is annual low-dose CT from 50 to 80 with a 20 pack-year history (2021). Cervical screening intervals are unchanged from 2018.

title: Screen for depression. Do not swap in a suicide score
lead: Screen adults for depression, including in pregnancy and after birth. A stand-alone suicide-risk questionnaire is an I statement, not a required screen.
lines: A positive depression screen needs a diagnostic interview. The form is not the diagnosis.
Ask about suicide when the interview or the patient's words open that door. That is care, not the population screen the task force declined to endorse.
Treatment follows the diagnosis. A refill of a benzodiazepine is not depression treatment.
miss: Checking a suicide-risk box on every chart and never asking the two depression questions.

source.name: USPSTF. Screening for Depression in Adults. Screening for Suicide Risk.
source.says: Depression screening in adults is recommended. The task force found insufficient evidence to recommend for or against screening all adults for suicide risk with a stand-alone instrument.

more.name: USPSTF. Suicide risk in adults and older adults.

title: Tell the patient the absolute risk
lead: Counsel with the absolute risk reduction. A relative reduction of half can be one event in a thousand.
lines: Number needed to treat is 1 divided by that absolute difference.
A confidence interval that includes no difference is not a reason to change practice by itself.
A surrogate marker moving is not the same as a heart attack being prevented.
miss: Telling a patient a drug cuts risk in half without saying half of what.

source.name: USPSTF. Breast cancer screening.
source.says: Screening recommendations are based on absolute benefits and harms. Relative reductions without the baseline risk mislead.

title: Stop lung screening 15 years after the last cigarette
lead: Stop annual lung-cancer screening when the patient has not smoked for 15 years, turns 81, or develops a condition that limits the benefit.
lines: The eligible patient is 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years.
A shared decision comes before the first scan, including the false positives.
A symptom such as coughing blood is not a screening scan. It is a diagnostic scan.
miss: Continuing yearly scans in an 84-year-old who quit 20 years ago.

source.name: USPSTF. Lung cancer screening.
source.says: Screening stops after 15 smoke-free years, after age 80, or when comorbidity removes the benefit.

title: Colon screening starts at 45 for average risk
lead: Average-risk colorectal screening starts at 45 and continues through 75. A first-degree relative with an early cancer starts earlier.
lines: Stool tests and colonoscopy are both acceptable. A positive stool test still needs a colonoscopy.
Ages 76 to 85 are an individual decision, not an automatic stop or an automatic start.
Iron deficiency in an older adult is a diagnostic colonoscopy, not a screening interval.
miss: Repeating a stool test after a positive one, instead of scoping.

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal cancer screening.
source.says: Average-risk screening begins at 45. A positive stool-based test is followed by colonoscopy.

title: Mammography is every other year from 40 through 74
lead: The USPSTF recommends mammography every other year from age 40 through 74. It does not recommend supplemental ultrasound for dense breasts as a proven add-on.
lines: Age 75 and older is an I statement. Decide with the patient.
A palpable mass is a diagnostic workup, not a screening interval.
A family history of a BRCA-associated cancer is a different, earlier plan.
miss: Telling a 42-year-old to wait until 50 because that used to be the start.

source.name: USPSTF. Breast cancer screening.
source.says: Biennial mammography from 40 through 74 is the recommendation. Supplemental imaging for density is not endorsed.

title: Cervical screening does not start before 21
lead: Cervical screening starts at 21. Ages 21 to 29 are cytology every 3 years. Ages 30 to 65 may use cytology every 3 years or high-risk HPV testing every 5.
lines: A vaccinated patient is still screened.
Yearly Pap smears are not the recommendation.
Bleeding after sex is a symptom and is examined now.
miss: Starting Pap smears at the first pelvic exam of a 16-year-old.

source.name: USPSTF. Cervical cancer screening.
source.says: Screening begins at 21. Intervals are every 3 years with cytology alone in younger women, with HPV options after 30.

title: A positive depression screen is an interview, not a prescription
lead: A positive depression screen is followed by a diagnostic interview. The form does not start a drug by itself.
lines: Screening is recommended in adults, including in pregnancy and after birth.
A stand-alone suicide-risk questionnaire for every adult is an I statement.
Ask about suicide when the interview opens that door. That is care.
miss: Prescribing an antidepressant from a score of 12 with no conversation.

source.name: USPSTF. Screening for Depression in Adults.
source.says: A positive screen requires a diagnostic assessment. It is not itself a diagnosis or a prescription.

title: Aspirin prevents preeclampsia only in the patients at high risk
lead: Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks prevents preeclampsia in patients with a high-risk condition. It does not treat a pressure of 170.
lines: Prior preeclampsia, multifetal pregnancy, chronic hypertension, diabetes, kidney disease, and autoimmune disease are the high-risk list.
The dose used in the recommendation is 81 mg.
Severe-range pressures are treated with antihypertensives and magnesium, not with aspirin.
miss: Starting aspirin at 34 weeks as the treatment of severe hypertension.

source.name: USPSTF. Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia.
source.says: Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks is for prevention in high-risk patients. It is not the treatment of severe-range blood pressure.

title: The four abilities, for this decision
lead: Capacity is the ability to decide this question today: to understand, appreciate, reason, and say a choice.
lines: It is decision-specific. A patient may refuse surgery and still be able to choose an antibiotic.
It can change with fever, sodium, drugs, and time. Recheck it. Do not stamp it on the chart forever.
Competence is the court's word. Capacity is the clinician's judgment.
miss: Calling a patient incapacitated because they disagreed with the recommended operation.

source.name: StatPearls. Competency and Capacity. Appelbaum, New England Journal of Medicine, 2007.
source.says: Clinical capacity requires understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and a choice, and it is judged for the decision at hand.

more.name: Appelbaum PS. Assessment of Patients' Competence to Consent to Treatment. N Engl J Med. 2007.

title: Tell the patient about the error
lead: A harmful error is disclosed to the patient: what happened, what it means, and what will be done next.
lines: Do not alter the record. Add a dated note.
An apology for the event is not a guess about legal fault.
Hiding the error, or telling only the family and not the patient who can hear it, fails the duty.
miss: Writing a vague note and hoping the next team explains it.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Disclosure of harmful error is an ethical duty. The record stays accurate, and the patient is told what happened.

title: The surrogate uses the patient's standard
lead: A surrogate's job is substituted judgment: what this patient would have chosen. Best interest is the fallback when that is unknown.
lines: The family's preference, the oldest child's preference, and the team's preference are not the standard.
A written directive and prior statements outrank a surrogate's new opinion.
If no one knows what the patient would have wanted, choose what serves the patient's interests.
miss: Doing what the loudest relative demands because they are present.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Decisions for Adult Patients Who Lack Capacity.
source.says: Surrogates decide according to the patient's previously expressed preferences, and according to the patient's best interest when preferences are unknown.

title: A capacitated refusal stands
lead: A patient with capacity may refuse treatment, including treatment that would save their life.
lines: Confirm the four abilities for this decision, and confirm they heard the consequence.
Document the refusal and the reasons. Offer to revisit it.
A relative cannot overrule that refusal.
miss: Sedating a refusing patient, or asking the family to sign, because the team is sure the patient is wrong.

source.name: StatPearls. Competency and Capacity.
source.says: A patient who has capacity for the decision may refuse care. Disagreement with the physician is not incapacity.

title: Consent is interpreted, not translated by the child
lead: A professional interpreter is used for consent when you and the patient do not share a language. A child or a family member is not the interpreter.
lines: Speak to the patient, not to the interpreter.
A short conversation in the hallway is not informed consent.
Document the interpreter's identity.
miss: Asking a 10-year-old to explain a surgery to a parent.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Qualified interpreters are required for informed consent. Family members, especially children, are not an acceptable substitute.

title: Emergency care proceeds when no one can consent
lead: If a patient cannot consent and no surrogate can be reached in time, emergency treatment that a reasonable person would want proceeds.
lines: This is implied consent for the emergency, not a blank check for elective procedures.
Keep looking for the surrogate while you treat.
Document why you could not wait.
miss: Withholding a life-saving procedure overnight because the family phone went to voicemail.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Emergency treatment under implied consent is appropriate when delay would cause serious harm and no decision-maker is available.

title: A do-not-resuscitate order is not a do-not-treat order
lead: A do-not-resuscitate order means you do not attempt resuscitation if the heart stops. Antibiotics, surgery, and comfort care are separate decisions.
lines: Ask what the order was meant to cover.
A patient can want surgery and refuse resuscitation.
Do not withhold pain medicine because a DNR is on the chart.
miss: Cancelling the antibiotics because the chart says DNR.

source.name: StatPearls. Advance Directives.
source.says: DNR limits resuscitation. It does not by itself limit other indicated treatment.

title: Withdrawing a ventilator is ethically the same as not starting it
lead: Stopping a treatment that is no longer wanted or no longer helps is ethically the same as never having started it.
lines: The goal is the patient's goal, not the team's discomfort.
Medicines for air hunger are given. The intent is comfort.
A slow wean that prolongs suffering to make the team feel better is not kinder.
miss: Refusing to stop a ventilator the patient never wanted because stopping feels like killing.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Withdrawal and withholding of life-sustaining treatment are ethically equivalent when the treatment no longer serves the patient's goals.

title: A capable patient may refuse blood
lead: A capable adult may refuse blood, including when refusal may be fatal. You explain the consequence and you honor the refusal.
lines: Make sure the refusal is for this surgery and this risk.
A surrogate does not get to impose a refusal the patient never made, or to overturn one the patient did.
Children are treated with blood when it is life-saving even if a parent refuses.
miss: Transfusing a clearly refusing capable adult because the hemoglobin is 5.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: A capable adult's refusal of transfusion is honored. Parental refusal does not block life-saving transfusion of a child.

title: Parents cannot refuse emergency care that saves a child
lead: Parents decide for a child except when refusal would cause death or serious harm. Then you treat and you involve the protective system.
lines: Explain, negotiate, and document.
An emergency is not the moment for a prolonged ethics debate.
Elective care is different from a life-saving transfusion or an emergency surgery.
miss: Watching a child deteriorate because a parent declined an emergency operation.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Parental authority does not extend to refusing emergency treatment needed to prevent death or serious harm.

title: A pregnant patient with capacity decides, including a refusal of cesarean
lead: A capable pregnant patient decides about cesarean delivery. The fetus does not give a separate veto that lets you operate against her refusal.
lines: Explain the fetal risk in plain words.
Coercion and a court order are not the routine path.
Document the conversation and continue to offer care.
miss: Taking a refusing patient to the operating room because the tracing is bad.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: A capable pregnant patient retains the right to refuse surgery. Fetal benefit does not erase that refusal.

title: Sterilization consent is not obtained during labor
lead: Consent for sterilization is obtained before labor, when the patient can deliberate. A signature between contractions is not adequate consent.
lines: Pain, fear, and a power imbalance make labor the wrong moment.
A prior wish is revisited before the procedure, not assumed.
Document the earlier conversation.
miss: Adding a tubal ligation to a cesarean because the patient nodded during a contraction.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Sterilization requires consent obtained outside the pressure of active labor.

title: The person doing the procedure obtains the consent
lead: Consent for a procedure is obtained by a clinician who understands the procedure and will participate. A student who has never done it does not obtain that consent alone.
lines: The patient is told who will be present and what a student will do.
A form signed for a different operation does not cover this one.
Questions are answered before the sedative is given.
miss: Sending a student who cannot explain the risks to get the signature.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: The clinician responsible for the procedure discloses the risks. Learners do not obtain consent beyond their knowledge.

title: A sensitive exam uses a chaperone
lead: A breast, pelvic, or genital exam is done with a chaperone offered and, in many settings, present. The patient's comfort is part of consent.
lines: Explain each step before you do it.
Stop if the patient withdraws consent.
A chaperone protects the patient and the clinician.
miss: Proceeding with a pelvic exam after the patient asked you to stop.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Sensitive examinations require explanation, the option of a chaperone, and consent that can be withdrawn.

title: Pain medicine at the end of life is not euthanasia
lead: Opioids given to treat pain or air hunger, even if they might hasten death, are not euthanasia when the intent is relief.
lines: The dose is the dose that relieves the symptom.
A dose chosen to kill is a different act.
Do not withhold morphine from a dying patient because of that confusion.
miss: Leaving a dying patient in pain to avoid a theoretical hastening of death.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: The principle of double effect permits symptom-relieving opioids when the intent is comfort and the dose is proportionate.

title: An impaired colleague is your problem
lead: If a colleague's impairment puts patients at risk, you act. Silence is not loyalty.
lines: Remove the colleague from the patient if the risk is immediate.
Report through the system your institution requires.
A rumor is not the same as an observed impairment. Act on what you know.
miss: Letting an intoxicated colleague finish the shift because confronting them is awkward.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Patient protection requires action when a colleague is impaired. Immediate risk is interrupted, and the impairment is reported.

title: Do not alter the record
lead: A late correction is added, dated, and signed. The original note is not deleted or rewritten after a bad outcome.
lines: An addendum says when you learned the new fact.
Changing a note to hide an error is a second harm.
The disclosure to the patient and the note tell the same story.
miss: Editing yesterday's note after the complication to make the plan look safer.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: The medical record is corrected by addendum. Altering the original entry after an adverse event is unethical.

title: Research consent is not clinical consent
lead: Enrolling a patient in research requires a research consent that explains the study, the alternatives, and the right to leave. The treatment consent does not cover it.
lines: The patient can decline the study and still receive care.
A power imbalance means you do not pressure.
The consent names what is experimental.
miss: Adding a research biopsy because the patient already signed the surgery consent.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Research participation requires a separate consent. Refusal does not affect standard care.

title: A placebo given as if it were treatment is a deception
lead: Giving a placebo while telling the patient it is an active drug is a deception. It is not a clever therapeutic trial.
lines: If a placebo is studied, the consent says so.
Symptoms still get a real evaluation.
Trust, once broken, ruins the next true recommendation.
miss: Prescribing a sugar pill for pain and calling it a strong analgesic.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Deceptive use of placebo violates informed consent. Placebo in research is disclosed.

title: Suspected child abuse is reported without a parent's permission
lead: Suspected child abuse is reported. You do not need the parent's permission, and you do not need proof.
lines: Treat the injury.
The report is to the agency the law names.
A parent who asks you not to report is the reason the duty does not sit with the parent.
miss: Agreeing to keep a suspicious fracture between you and the family.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Clinicians report suspected child abuse. Parental consent is not required, and certainty is not the threshold.

title: Organ donation is asked separately from the decision to stop support
lead: The treating team does not couple the request for organs to the moment they recommend stopping support. A designated requester has that conversation.
lines: The decision to stop is the patient's or the surrogate's, made on its own merits.
A conflict of interest is avoided by separating the roles.
The patient who wanted to donate still can. The timing of the ask is what changes.
miss: Saying you will stop the ventilator if the family agrees to donation.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: The decision to withdraw support is independent of organ donation. A designated requester handles the donation conversation.

title: A POLST is an order. An advance directive is a statement
lead: A POLST or similar portable order tells emergency clinicians what to do tonight. An advance directive tells a surrogate what the patient would have wanted.
lines: They are not interchangeable.
A capable patient can change either.
Emergency personnel follow the order they can see.
miss: Ignoring a POLST that says do not intubate because an old advance directive was vague.

source.name: StatPearls. Advance Directives.
source.says: Portable medical orders direct emergency treatment. Advance directives guide surrogates and are not the same document.

title: Against-medical-advice discharge still gets an explanation
lead: A capable patient may leave against advice. You explain the risk, treat what you still can, and document. You do not punish the patient by withholding a prescription they need for a safe exit.
lines: Confirm capacity for this decision.
Offer to treat the dangerous problem before they go.
A signature is not required for you to have had the conversation, and refusal to sign is documented.
miss: Refusing to give a needed antibiotic because the patient is leaving against advice.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: A capable patient may leave. The risks are explained, indicated bridging treatment is offered, and the conversation is documented.

title: You do not offer a treatment that cannot work
lead: You do not offer a menu of interventions that cannot achieve the patient's goal. Futility is explained, and comfort is offered.
lines: The word is used carefully. A treatment that is unlikely is not the same as one that cannot work.
A second opinion is reasonable. A false hope is not.
The family is not asked to choose among useless options.
miss: Asking a family whether they want chest compressions that cannot restore a dead circulation, as if it were a real choice.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Interventions that cannot achieve a physiologic goal are not offered as choices. Comfort care is offered instead.

title: A scarce bed follows a rule you could defend in public
lead: When two patients need one bed or one drug, the rule is clinical and stated in advance. Friendship, fame, and anger do not move the list.
lines: Tell both patients the truth you can tell.
Document the reason.
The same rule applies on the next shift.
miss: Giving the last ICU bed to a colleague's relative who is less sick.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Scarce resources are allocated by a consistent clinical rule, not by personal relationship.
